title: Senior Frontend Engineer
description:
Senior Frontend Engineer 

Remote (UK-based) | Full-Time 

About Us 

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year ( Risk.net ). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 60+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role 

We're looking for a senior full-stack engineer to build the trading platform our clients use every day. Despite the "frontend" name, this is not a UI-only role — our Frontend team works across the whole application stack in TypeScript and Rust, from the trader-facing interfaces down to the services behind them. It's distinct from our Backend team, who own the low-latency C++/Go trading engine.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who takes on the hardest problems and delivers them under their own steam. You'll own complex, ambiguous, performance-critical work end-to-end — designed, built, tested, deployed, and supported in production. You lead through code, craft, and mentoring, setting the technical example the rest of the team calibrates to. This is not a role where you write code and throw it over a wall: our engineers own the full lifecycle, and when something breaks, you're part of the team that investigates and fixes it.

Occasional hours outside the normal working day are required for production releases, scheduled maintenance windows, and Level 3 support during critical incidents. We keep this to a minimum and recognise the commitment — but owning a production trading platform means being there when it matters.

What You'll Work On 

- Complex full-stack features in TypeScript and Rust — from trader-facing interfaces to the application services behind them

- Real-time market-data presentation and high-throughput, low-latency application code across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency

- React and reactive state management (RX, MobX, or similar) for demanding, data-dense trading interfaces

- Distributed systems and real-time data over REST, WebSockets, and network protocols

- Architecture and solution design for the hardest technical problems the team faces

- Observability and monitoring — dashboards, alerting, and metrics that make frontend behaviour visible

- Production systems that handle real money — reliability is not optional

What We Need 

Technical: 

- Strong full-stack engineering ability with deep TypeScript / JavaScript (ES6+) (5+ years)

- Solid experience with React and reactive state management (RX, MobX, or similar)

- Working knowledge of Rust , or the clear appetite and ability to get there — it's part of our stack

- Strong grasp of distributed systems, API design, and real-time data (REST, WebSockets, network protocols such as TCP/UDP and binary protocols)

- Comfortable reasoning about architecture and making defensible technical trade-offs

- Python for scripting, automation, and tooling is a bonus

- Git and Linux fundamentals

- Experience in financial services or trading technology is a plus but not essential

How you work: 

- You ship. You're delivery-focused — you iterate, you improve, you get things into production

- You run with things. Give you an ambiguous, complex problem and you drive it to done without being managed through it. Senior here means trusted, not just experienced

- You have range. You're not just strong in the familiar parts of the stack — you pick up the unfamiliar and hold your own on the hardest work

- You own it. When you build something, you take responsibility for its behaviour in production. You respond to incidents (15-minute acknowledgement SLA during working hours), investigate issues, and close the loop

- You raise the bar. You review peers' work thoughtfully, mentor the engineers around you through the craft, and set a standard others calibrate to

- You write things down. Documentation is not an afterthought — it's how we scale knowledge across a distributed team. If it's not written down, it doesn't exist

- You communicate. We're a distributed team across multiple time zones. Clear, proactive communication — especially when things go wrong — is essential

- You embrace AI tooling. We use AI tools (Claude, Gemini) to amplify our engineering capability — from code review and debugging to incident investigation and documentation. You don't need to be an expert, but you should be curious and willing to learn

What You Get 

- Real problems — trading systems where performance is measured in microseconds, not user clicks

- An excellent team — senior engineers who care about craft, collaborate openly, and hold each other to high standards

- Ownership — small teams, clear accountability, direct impact on the platform and our clients

- Competitive package — up to 30 days leave + bank holidays, private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites

- Remote-friendly — work from home with flexibility. We trust our people to deliver

- Sustainable pace — we work hard, but we don't burn people out. Balance is how we stay sharp

- Growth — career progression to senior roles, performance specialisation, or technical leadership. We invest in people who invest in us

We believe in transparency, honest feedback, and writing things down. We celebrate delivery, not activity. We frame AI as empowering people — removing toil, amplifying capability, enabling higher-value work.

We aim to build systems that don't depend on the heroics of individuals to maintain and support — systems and processes that are resilient, documented, and sustainable.

Our Hiring Process 

We keep our process focused and respectful of your time. Our process follows three stages.

Stage 1: Initial Conversation with Talent Acquisition
Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes

Stage 2: Hiring Manager Conversation with the relevant team lead or hiring manager
Format: Video call, ~60 minutes

Stage 3: Technical Interview with two members of the relevant engineering team
Format: Video call, interactive session, ~60 minutes

What to expect in each stage will be explained by Talent Acquisition if you're invited to interview. Throughout the process, we aim to keep momentum with no unnecessary delays between stages, and feedback typically comes within a few business days.

*Please note that depending on availability, Stage 2 and 3 may swap around.

How to Apply 

Please apply directly via this job posting — all applications, including those submitted via LinkedIn, are managed through our applicant tracking system, so you'll always land in the same place regardless of where you found this role.

Right to Work: Candidates must have the existing right to work in the UK. We are not currently able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Equal Opportunities: Reactive Markets is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

Reasonable Adjustments: If you need any adjustments or support during the application or interview process, please let us know — we're happy to accommodate.

Data Protection: By applying, you consent to Reactive Markets processing your personal data for recruitment purposes, in line with our privacy policy .

- Build and maintain observability for ML systems: infrastructure and model health via Datadog, and evaluation/quality signals via Braintrust, catching regressions before they reach users.

- Work hand in hand with AI inference engineers on the shared foundations of our self-hosted LLM stack (model registry, deployment automation, shared GPU capacity), and stay current with MLOps practices for classic ML, generative AI and agentic systems alike.

Who you are

Before you read on: if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

- Have prior experience as an MLOps Engineer, Cloud Engineer for ML applications, AI Infrastructure Engineer, or Platform Engineer for AI, or in a similar role

- Have hands-on experience with Kubernetes in production and GitOps tools (e.g. ArgoCD), and have built MLOps pipelines for containerizing models and solutions with Docker

- Have hands-on experience with Kubernetes-native agent abstractions (CRDs/operators, e.g. kagent) or building production agent runtimes

- Have experience with ML model quantization and optimization

- Have experience with GPU sharing/partitioning technologies (e.g. NVIDIA MIG, time-slicing, MPS)

Life at Doctolib Tech

title: Staff Backend Software Engineer
description:
About Notabene 

Notabene is on a mission to make crypto a part of the everyday economy. Leading crypto organizations use our tools to reduce transaction risk and make crypto transfers safe. Working across three continents in eight countries, the Notabene team serves our fantastic community of 100+ customers, including financial institutions, fintechs, exchanges, and more. Our co-founders spearheaded foundational Self Sovereign Identity protocols and use-cases. This technology is key to the internals of our cutting edge tech stack.

We’re proud to have the support of leading investors, including Y Combinator, Jump Capital, Castle Island, Green Visor Capital, and more.

We’re at an exhilarating moment in our journey, as regulation technologies (reg-techs) are fast becoming recognized as a vital enabler of the crypto ecosystem. Notabene is growing fast—and we’re looking for people like you to help shape the future rails of the crypto industry!

The Impact You'll Have: 

Every crypto transfer we touch moves between institutions that run their own systems, answer to different regulators, and have no reason to trust each other. The software in the middle has to be right every time. A message processed twice, a lost update, or a record shown to the wrong tenant is a compliance failure for our customers.

You’ll work on the core platform that carries this data between institutions around the world, written in Go.

As a Staff Engineer on the team you’ll build the hardest parts of it, contribute to its design, and help the engineers around you do their best work.

What You'll Do 

- 
Design and build core parts of our transaction platform.

- 
Build for correctness under failure, with the isolation and auditability a regulated product needs.

- 
Scale the platform as transaction volume and the number of institutions per node grow, keeping latency predictable and the database healthy.

- 
Write design docs for what you build, and give sharp, useful reviews on other people’s designs and code.

- 
Build with AI agents every day, and help improve the specs, context and review practices that make agent-written code safe to ship in a regulated product.

- 
Work with product, compliance and customer-facing teams to turn regulatory and customer needs into working software.

- 
Own what you ship in production, from tracing and alerts to incident follow-ups.

- 
Mentor engineers on the team.

- 
Work on an on call rotation

Must Haves 

- 
Systems design depth. You’ve designed and owned distributed systems where correctness matters more than features. You know asynchronous processing well and can reason about what happens when parts of it fail.

- 
Strong Go, or deep production experience in another statically typed backend language (Java, Kotlin, Rust, C#) and the appetite to be shipping Go within your first weeks.

- 
PostgreSQL in depth: schema design, query plans, locking and isolation levels, migrations on live systems, and multi-tenant data.

- 
End-to-end ownership in the cloud. Working knowledge of AWS or GCP: IAM, networking, managed databases, queues and storage. You can read and change Terraform and debug production from traces and logs.

- 
AI-native engineering. You use coding agents such as Claude Code or Cursor every day and can show how. You write the specs and context, break work down for them, and review their output as hard as a human pull request. You know where they fail.

- 
Staff-level experience. A track record of delivering large, technically hard projects end to end and helping the engineers around you get better. Typically 8+ years building backend systems.

- 
Clear, concise writing in a remote company that makes decisions in documents and async threads.

- 
Security fundamentals for sensitive data: encryption in transit and at rest, key handling, minimising personal data, and least-privilege access.

Nice-to-Haves 

- 
Applied cryptography: encryption, signing and key management.

- 
Decentralized identity: DIDs, verifiable credentials, DIDComm.

- 
Regulated finance, payments or compliance: Travel Rule, AML, ISO 20022.

- 
Building and running software under SOC 2 or ISO 27001 controls.

- 
Crypto and blockchain knowledge: chains, addresses, assets, CAIP identifiers.

- 
Node.js and TypeScript.

- 
Queue and workflow systems, and modern observability tooling.

Benefits 

- 
Flexible Remote Work: Work from anywhere!

- 
$1000 WFH Stipend: Use within your first year of employment.

- 
MacBook Pro: Procured by you and your manager to find a model that meets your needs.

- 
Unlimited PTO: We trust you to take as much holiday as you need.

- 
Country-Specific Benefits: Statutory offerings and contributions, managed via our employer-of-record.

Apply Today! 

If you strongly believe this role is for you, please apply. Notabene considers a broad array of candidates, including those without blockchain experience. Whether you’re returning to work after a gap in employment, or taking the next step in your career path, we will be glad to have you on our radar. 

Notabene is proud to be an equal employment workplace and an affirmative action employer. By valuing inclusion and diversity of all forms, we strictly prohibit and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, ancestry, citizenship, sexual orientation, status as a protected veteran, or any other legally protected characteristic.

title: Product Engineer, UK
description:
Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs. 

🚀 Our Story

Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists and AI at Partly .

🖍️ This role

This is a product-builder role, not a ticket-taking one. You own a product surface end to end: you talk to the customer, form the idea, build it, ship it, measure it, and decide what happens next. The same person who understands the repairer writes the code. There is no handoff for product quality to leak through.

You'll build at the center of a multi-trillion-dollar industry that still runs on phone calls, spreadsheets, and tribal knowledge. Replacement parts is one of the largest physical markets on earth and one of the least digitised, and there is no established playbook to copy. Partly is creating the category.

Our moat is Interpreter, a domain-specific AI model that understands parts, vehicles, and the messy real-world relationships between them in ways general-purpose models cannot. It is what lets software finally make sense of a physical, offline industry, and it is the engine underneath everything you build.

And what you build is changing shape. We are not bolting AI onto old screens. We are creating genuinely new agentic experiences for a broad spectrum of users, from estimators and parts managers to accountants and suppliers, where people express intent and supervise outcomes while agents handle the mechanical work. Designing how that trust is earned, surface by surface, while each one still delivers value today, is the heart of the role.

You'll work at an inflection point in how software itself gets built. AI-assisted development has collapsed the distance between an idea and a working version of it. The builders we want already work this way: they prototype in an afternoon, put it in front of real customers within days, and read the signal themselves. We want someone who works like that now, or is visibly building toward it.

💻 What will you do

- Build, not just specify. Prototype new product iterations yourself using AI-assisted and LLM-assisted tooling, fast, disposable, real. Treat the prototype as the hypothesis and put it in front of real customers before writing the spec. Ship production code, instrument it, and watch how it actually gets used.

- Stay close to customers. Spend time where the work happens. Understand what estimators, parts managers, and others actually do, where they lose time, and what better would feel like. This is a core weekly activity, not an occasional input.

- Reconcile signal. Combine what you see with what the data says, and reconcile the two when they disagree. Turn that understanding straight into what you build next.

- Own the outcome. Steer by your surface's metrics; adoption and value delivered are yours. Make the call on priority and explain the reasoning, especially when the answer is no. When something is broken, own it, diagnose it precisely, and fix it.

- Make the trade-off. Weigh product impact against engineering effort in the same breath, and find the cheaper path to the same outcome.

- Build the agentic experience. Move your surface from manual operation toward supervised delegation: capture intent, decide where the human stays in the loop, and earn trust step by step so users never lose the thread of a high-stakes job.

- Hold the craft. The surface feels fast, clear, and considered. You push back when something does not feel right, even when it technically works.

- Raise the bar. Pair with SW Engineers on the harder systems work behind your surface, and contribute beyond your boundary: shared components, product craft, and what excellent building looks like here as the team grows.

- 

🥷 Your skills

Non-negotiables 

- You ship end to end: a track record of taking features from idea to production, code included, with clear accountability for whether they worked. Roughly 3+ years building and shipping software in production.

- Genuine customer obsession: a real habit of spending time with users in their work context, with a track record of that depth driving what you build.

- Product taste and craft: the bar is experiences that feel effortless to time-pressured, non-technical users across fragmented, high-stakes workflows. Functional is not the finish line.

- A point of view on agentic product design: how an experience moves from manual operation to supervised delegation, and how automation earns user trust gradually rather than all at once.

- You build rapid prototypes yourself, with AI-assisted tools as a first instinct for testing an idea.

- Solid full-stack engineering with a frontend lean: production-quality code and sound fundamentals. Systems-specialist depth is not the point of the role.

- Trade-off fluency: you weigh product impact against engineering effort and often find a cheaper route to the same result.

- Strong analytical instinct: you define the metric, build the view, read it, and act, without waiting for a data team.

- You operate well in ambiguity and autonomy, and shape the problem rather than waiting for a spec.

Strong signals we look for 

- Shipped AI-assisted or agent-driven features in production, particularly where the human stays in the loop.

- Built for a multi-persona, operational, or workflow-heavy B2B product.

- Founder background, or early employee at a startup that scaled materially.

- You've killed or radically changed something you personally believed in, and can explain why.

Bonus 

- Domain knowledge in automotive, the parts aftermarket, repair, or insurance claims.

- Marketplace or network experience, from the demand or supply side.

- Rust, or genuine eagerness to learn it. It is part of our stack.

Please note: if you don't have all the skills or experience listed above but believe you could be outstanding in this role, please still consider applying. Many people count themselves out. We'd love the chance to learn more about you and why you're exceptional. 

🪅 Benefits 

- Competitive base salary + equity . We offer competitive salaries and generous equity options for all full-time employees, ensuring everyone shares in the financial upside when we win.

- Annual global offsite in New Zealand . Travel with the rest of the UK and EU team as we gather and connect for 1-2 weeks at our product and engineering hub in Christchurch.

- Parental leave: Primary caregivers receive 3 months of fully paid parental leave, plus a flexible return-to-work (four days on full pay for your first three months back).

- Team lunches: Lunch provided daily (Monday to Friday) in the office

- Flexible working hours: We have flexible working hours and default to working from the office.

- Season openers & events: We host regular events, including quarterly "season openers" for our UK/EU team, monthly team catch-ups, and weekly happy hours.

- Healthy body, healthy mind: Every team member gets a £750 annual wellness allowance on a Partly-branded card. Use on gym memberships, rock climbing, physio, massage, GP visits, prescriptions; anything that you or your family, need.

title: Fullstack Engineer - Mid Level - Actions Team
description:
About Staffbase 

We inspire people to achieve great things together. Our mission is to help organizations unlock the power of inspirational communication with the first AI-native Employee Experience Platform . Our industry-leading and award-winning agentic AI communications channels - intranet, employee app and email solutions - create engaging experiences that connect and empower employees.

Headquartered in Chemnitz, Germany and New York City, with offices in Berlin, London, Sydney, Tokyo, Prague, and Minneapolis–St. Paul, our diverse team of 550+ employees supports 1,500+ customers—reaching over 14 million employees—in transforming their employee experience.
We are proud to be a Unicorn company—privately valued at over $1 billion—demonstrating strong growth, innovation, and lasting impact in our industry. Together, we’re shaping the future of workplace communication.

We're looking for a Fullstack Engineer to join our Actions team in building the core infrastructure that powers our plugin platform. You'll create the UI components, integration layers, and security mechanisms that enable our customers to extend the platform with custom integrations while maintaining safety and flexibility across our 1,500+ customer base. This is essential infrastructure work that shapes how our customers scale their integrations. 

Our environment 

- Working with skilled and like-minded professionals in a team that values diversity and inclusivity 

- We aim to create a flexible and agile work environment that promotes the well-being and work-life balance of our employees 

- We believe that team events during working hours play a vital role in building an exceptionally effective team, and we encourage them 

- We are enthusiastic about technology and committed to using it to improve the world 

- We follow the “You build it, you run it” approach and take pride in it 

The Team 

The Actions team sits at the heart of Staffbase's AI ambitions. We're the team that gives Navigator — our AI assistant and the main entry point into Staffbase — the ability to actually do things: submit a form, complete a task inside an integration, or take an action on a user's behalf through the agent. If Navigator is the brain, we build the hands. 

That means two big things. First, we enrich what the AI can see and act on, our plugins, our widgets and the wider Staffbase platform so the assistant can do real work, not just talk about it. Second, we build the extensions that connect to the tools people already use, like Workday, Personio, ServiceNow and Microsoft.   We're not just shipping features, though. A core part of our mission is building the extensibility framework that lets others build too.   

What you'll be doing 

- Building a UI component library that generated apps can assemble from, turning components like payslip views and approval flows into maintained, reusable pieces instead of regenerated artifacts 

- Creating the connection layer between generated apps and customer source systems—HR platforms, time-tracking and scheduling systems, and a long tail of vendors with thin or undocumented APIs 

- Defining extension points (widgets, menus, sidebars) so plugins declare where they surface and what they connect to in a single, clean configuration 

- Designing and implementing a cross-integration authentication solution that lets customers run multiple integrations without forcing employees to log in repeatedly 

- Shipping plugins on the platform yourself, staying a consumer of what we build so we catch gaps early 

What you need to be successful 

- Strong knowledge of React and TypeScript for frontend work, Kotlin or Go and TypeScript experience for backend services 

- Real experience integrating third-party APIs, especially the challenging ones—inconsistent auth, partial documentation, legacy and on-prem systems 

- Deep understanding of multi-tenancy security and data isolation; you care about scope checks and preventing cross-tenant leaks 

- Good judgment about what to standardize and what to leave flexible—drawing that line in the right place is central to this role 

Nice to have experience  

- You are comfortable with edge and serverless runtimes like Cloudflare Workers 

- You have built a plugin system, SDK, or developer platform before 

- Developed a design system or component library that other teams depended on 

- Real-world experience with OAuth and enterprise SSO 

- Experience treating AI code generation as a product surface, not just a personal tool 

What you'll get 

- Competitive Compensation - we offer attractive salary packages including LTIP (unit-based Long Term Incentive Plan)

- Flexibility - we offer flexible working time models and the option of hybrid work, and support this with a yearly flex work allowance of €1560 

- Recharge - with 31 vacation days annually (incl. one floating holiday), plus pro rata fully paid Fridays off during August

- Support - we offer offering a company pension scheme 

- Volunteers Day - you’ll get one day off per year for supporting a social project

description:
You'll ship agents that move money, and you'll keep the rhythm that gets them shipped. Accounts payable, accounts receivable, treasury: autonomous agents that read the invoice, match it, negotiate the discount, release the payment, and reconcile the cash. Every one of those actions runs in production with a customer's CFO watching the result.

Most of what the industry calls engineering culture was written for a world where humans typed every line. That world ended. We want to build the 2026 version: engineers who work with agents as a matter of course, where the unit of work is the loop (spec, generate, evaluate, correct, ship) rather than the ticket, where code review means reviewing the evals and prompts as hard as the diff, and where a regression suite over real customer invoices is what lets us move fast on systems that touch money. Nobody has a settled playbook for this. You'll help write ours, from inside a pod.

This is a player-coach role. You'll spend most of your week shipping code in one of our pods, and you'll manage the engineers day to day: 1:1s, feedback, growth, the hard conversation when it's needed. The rest goes to the delivery rhythm: pods commit to milestones in Linear, post progress daily, and review misses every Friday with the Head of Product and the CTO. You run that review and the follow-ups. The management share grows as we go from 8 engineers to 16 and beyond; this role is the natural path to Head of Engineering. You'll report to the CTO. Causa Prima is built by the team behind Taulia and backed by Creandum.

What you'll do 

- Ship as a senior engineer, 70 to 80% of your week. Take the hardest work in your pod, unblock the integration nobody wants, and review the code that touches money personally. You set the bar by clearing it in front of the team.

- Manage the engineers day to day. Weekly 1:1s, direct feedback, growth plans, and the honest conversation about who's ready for more scope and who's in the wrong seat. The CTO owns hiring decisions and the technical direction; the people in the pods are yours.

- Run the delivery rhythm. Weekly milestone commitments, the Friday review, the dashboard of committed versus delivered, and the follow-ups when something slips. Misses are discussed to learn, not to blame; your job is that they get discussed at all, with an owner and a next step.

- Make the loop the way we work. Specs written so an agent can execute them, evals that run before merge, review practices that treat prompts as code. The CTO owns the architecture; you own that every pod actually works this way, including the change management when they don't.

- Raise risk early. You know on Tuesday what won't make Friday, and so does everyone who needs to.

- Sit with customers. Controllers explaining why the agent's match was technically correct and operationally wrong. AP leads walking you through an SAP extension nobody documented. That's where the next milestone comes from.

What we're looking for 

- A senior engineer who likes the operational side. You've shipped production systems where mistakes cost money: fintech, payments, ERP-adjacent, enterprise B2B. You've also managed engineers, run their 1:1s and a delivery cadence, and liked it enough to want more of it while still writing code.

- You build with agents. You've shipped something in the last month using an agentic coding tool that saved you a week, and you can show us. Python or TypeScript in anger, and enough PostgreSQL to review a migration without asking.

- You've kept commitments reliable before, with numbers. Committed versus shipped, cycle time, whatever you tracked. You've followed up on slipped work without it turning into a blame exercise.

- Minimal process instincts. You add a ritual when it earns its place and remove it when it doesn't. A weekly review that takes 30 minutes, not 90.

- You can disagree with a founder and stay in the room. We hire for trust and challenge in that order.

- Fluent English. German or Spanish is a plus. Munich preferred, Madrid works. You'll be in both offices regularly.

This is a wishlist, not a checklist. If the role excites you but you don't tick every box, we would encourage you to apply anyway.

Nice to have 

- AI agents in production, as the product rather than a feature.

- Depth in purchase-to-pay or order-to-cash, or scar tissue from an SAP integration.

- You've grown with a team through a Series A or B.

- Former founder or founding engineer.

title: Cloud Systems Administrator
description:
Headquarters: 

URL: https://oneimaging.com 

Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam.

The Systems Administrator owns the day-to-day administration of our SaaS and cloud vendor stack, with security and logging as the first priority. You will manage user access across every platform we use, keep audit logging and security controls configured and reviewed, write scripts to automate repetitive admin work, and act as a first responder on security incidents. You will also provide hands-on IT support to employees. This is a generalist role for someone who likes owning systems end to end: you are the person who knows how each vendor is set up, who has access to what, and where the logs live. 

What you'll do: 

Vendor and SaaS administration (security and logging first) 

- Serve as the primary administrator for our SaaS and cloud platforms: tenant settings, SSO/SAML and SCIM integration, MFA enforcement, API keys, roles and permissions.

- Configure and maintain audit logging on every platform that supports it; centralize logs where possible and make sure retention meets our compliance needs.

- Run periodic access reviews, remove stale accounts and over-privileged roles, and keep an accurate inventory of who has admin rights where.

- Own the security posture of each vendor: review security settings on new tools before rollout, track vendor security notices, and evaluate new vendor requests for risk.

User lifecycle and identity

- Onboard and offboard employees and contractors across all systems the same day, driven from Rippling and Google Workspace, our identity sources of truth.

- Manage groups, roles and licenses; keep license counts right-sized and flag waste.

- Maintain device enrollment, MDM policies and endpoint security for company laptops.

Scripting and automation

- Write and maintain scripts (Python, PowerShell, Bash) and use vendor APIs to automate provisioning, access reviews, log collection and reporting.

- Build lightweight integrations between systems (for example, HRIS to identity provider to SaaS) so manual admin work shrinks over time.

Security incident response

- Act as a first responder on security alerts: triage, contain (disable accounts, revoke tokens, isolate devices), gather evidence from logs, and escalate.

- Participate in post-incident reviews and implement the fixes that come out of them.

- Help maintain and test our incident response and business continuity runbooks.

IT support

- Provide tier 1–2 support to employees: hardware, accounts, access, video conferencing, printers and office network.

- Procure, image and manage laptops and peripherals; keep an asset inventory current.

- Write and keep up internal how-to documentation so common requests become self-service.

Platforms you will administer

These are our largest software and cloud vendors by spend over the last 12 months. Deep experience with the first group is expected; the rest you will pick up on the job.

Area

Platforms

Cloud infrastructure

Amazon Web Services (IAM, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Security Hub)

Identity, HR and devices

Rippling (HRIS, SSO, device management) and Google Workspace, used together as our identity source of truth

Productivity and email

Google Workspace (admin console, Vault, security center)

Customer support and CRM

Zendesk, Salesforce, Intercom

Communications

Zoom, Aircall, Twilio

Data and engineering

Databricks, MongoDB Atlas, Sentry, Linear, Postman, Stytch

AI platforms

Anthropic, OpenAI (API key and usage management)

Collaboration and design

Notion, Lucid, Figma, Adobe, Scribe

Security tools

NordVPN Teams, Virtru (email encryption)

Healthcare operations

Waystar, AdvancedMD

Marketing and recruiting

Braze, ActiveCampaign, Greenhouse, LinkedIn

About you: 

- 3+ years administering SaaS and cloud platforms in a company of 50–500 people, including Google Workspace and an identity/HR platform like Rippling or Okta, and ideally AWS.

- Hands-on experience configuring SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, MFA policies and role-based access.

- Working knowledge of audit logging and log review: you know what a CloudTrail event, a Workspace audit log or a Zendesk audit entry looks like and what to do with it.

- Scripting ability in at least one of Python, PowerShell or Bash, and comfort calling REST APIs.

- Experience responding to security incidents (phishing, compromised accounts, lost devices) and documenting what happened.

- Strong IT support instincts: you communicate clearly with non-technical colleagues and close tickets fast.

- Familiarity with HIPAA or a comparable compliance framework (SOC 2, ISO 27001) and what it means for access control and logging.

Nice to have:

- AWS Certified SysOps Administrator, Security Specialty, or Google Workspace Administrator certification.

- Experience with a SIEM or log aggregation tool (Datadog, Splunk, Google SecOps, or similar) and writing detection rules.

- MDM experience (Rippling, Jamf, Kandji, Intune) and macOS/Windows endpoint hardening.

- Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code for managing AWS and SaaS configuration.

- Prior work in a healthcare or other regulated company.

- Experience administering API usage and keys for AI platforms (Anthropic, OpenAI) and setting spend and access controls.

- Regression Coverage – Execute cross-platform regression testing prior to releases to ensure stability.

- Issue Investigation – Diagnose defects using logs, network tools, and API inspection techniques.

- Defect Lifecycle Management – Document, prioritize, and track defects while partnering with engineers on root-cause resolution.

- Environment Management – Maintain test environments, device coverage, and reliable platform test data.

- Risk Identification – Proactively surface quality risks during sprint planning and release cycles.

Here’s What You’ll Need To Be Successful:

- API Validation Expertise – Strong experience validating RESTful APIs and backend business logic.

- SDLC/STLC Knowledge – Solid understanding of software and testing lifecycle best practices.

- Testing Tool Proficiency – Hands-on experience with API testing tools such as Postman (or similar platforms).

- Technical Acumen – Ability to understand system architecture, integrations, and data flow.

- Startup Adaptability – Comfortable operating in a remote, fast-paced, and evolving environment.

- Ownership Mindset – High level of accountability with strong independent execution.

- Clear Communication – Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.

Interview Process:

- Your application will be reviewed for possible next steps by the Hiring Manager.

- If you meet eligibility requirements, the next step would be a video interview with a member of the PeopleOps team for about thirty (30) minutes.

- If warranted, the next step would be a technical video interview with our QA Lead and QA Engineer for one (1) hour

We're working at the frontier of autonomous systems, building agents that don't just chat, but run entire businesses.

Our system identifies business opportunities through market signals, validates ideas with live ad tests, builds and launches software products, and brings in human experts wherever agents fall short. That loop already runs end to end: from idea to launched product to first revenue.

Over the next 12 months, our focus is on reliability, throughput, and self-improvement, making every launch better than the last.

We're looking for a hands-on AI Engineer to take ownership of the architecture and development of our autonomous agent system.

You'll lead the technical direction of the platform, building multi-agent orchestration systems, self-improving agent harnesses, and AI-powered backend services. This is a highly technical leadership role that combines architectural decision-making with hands-on engineering.

- Write production code, particularly around agent runtime and orchestration.

- Debug and improve AI behavior in production through prompt engineering, structured outputs, retries, and fallbacks.

- Break down complex technical challenges into actionable milestones and prioritize the engineering roadmap.

- Establish engineering standards around code reviews, testing, observability, and release processes.

- Lead and support the engineering team while remaining deeply involved in implementation.

- Previous technical leadership experience at an early-stage company (Founding Engineer, Tech Lead, Head of Engineering, or similar).

- Strong backend engineering skills, including designing and maintaining APIs, services, and data flows.

- Experience with Vercel AI SDK, Claude Agent SDK, or building custom agent runtimes.

- Experience with PostgreSQL, Supabase, and pgvector.

- Familiarity with background job systems such as Inngest or Pub/Sub.

- Experience with Zod, Vitest, and GCP Cloud Run.

- Experience growing or restructuring distributed engineering teams.

- Interest in AI evaluation, safety, and observability.

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

What you’ll do

As a member of the team, the Solutions Architect will build highly consultative trusted relationships with c-level executives and technical decision makers in the customer’s organization to provide business and technical thought leadership, and become a trusted advisor in solving mission-critical business challenges. She/he will architect business models with them so they can drive new monetization opportunities and growth for both the user and Stripe. 

Responsibilities

- Be a key member of a Stripe account team with deep involvement in defining the customer strategy

- Identify and close new complex opportunities, and accelerate solution adoption. Understand and align with the customer’s product and business roadmap and uncover opportunities for Stripe to accelerate their progress on that roadmap.

- Work to deeply understand the customer’s business objectives, and then design and apply Stripe’s solutions to their challenges. Develop and articulate the end to end customer transformation journey and create future roadmaps and architectures with deep 3rd party integrations in play.

- Conduct business analysis and background research on customers, industries, and competitors with a view to support growth for the user's business. 

- Lead strategy engagements with users to align to business priorities, design solutions and secure the technical win by performing in-depth customer discovery, evangelizing the proposed solutions through executive briefings, readouts, presentations, workshops and solution demos. 

- Expand Stripe’s footprint within existing accounts to new global markets and business units by introducing new capabilities and local payment methods.

- Act as the “Voice of the Customer” to bring insights, trends and opportunities to the leadership, product and engineering teams from the forefront and prioritized for delivery. 

- Participate in sales forecasting, Quarterly Business Reviews and account/territory planning to strategically and tactically align for success

- Approximately 25% travel is anticipated to help you connect in-person in a meaningful way with users and collaborate internally

Who you are

You have achieved an experienced position as an enterprise architect, senior solution architect or principal solution engineer and have a successful track record advising enterprise-grade digital native / SAAS / Platform / Marketplace companies, focused on identifying business priorities, formulating technology strategies and designing an end-to-end business solution. You possess deep technical acumen, high interpersonal and leadership skills, and have demonstrated the ability to become a trusted advisor to senior executives and facilitate customer success along the entire customer journey. Strategic and creative thinker who can proactively identify challenges, take ownership, and maintain a positive approach when facing difficult obstacles.

- Executive engagement skills and presence, with an ability to establish strong relationships with key decision makers and build credibility at all levels.

- Effective group-facilitation skills and confidence in proposing and leading customer meetings to gain strategic footing and pursue opportunities.

- Passion to take on ownership and drive change in a constantly evolving environment. 

- Superior verbal and written communication skills in English

- Ability to travel per business needs

Preferred requirements

- Prior experience in consulting

- Experience at a growth stage internet/software company

title: Senior Data Scientist
description:
About us 

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels. 

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Trainline Data Science & Analytics Team 👋 
Data Science & Analytics (DSA) sits at the heart of how Trainline understands and improves the end-to-end customer journey, from finding a journey through to booking. Our data scientists and analysts work closely together to support supply, search and commerce, spotting patterns that affect the customer experience, identifying opportunities for our customers and our business, and building solutions that make life easier for the wider team.

This role offers the chance to work across multiple areas of the business rather than being confined to a single specialism, giving you real breadth and the opportunity to see how different parts of the customer journey connect.

As a Senior Data Scientist, you will take ownership of investigations and solutions that span search, supply and commerce, working with detailed datasets and linking data sources to support projects across pillars. You will collaborate closely with all teams responsible for core customer experiences (from Data, Product, Engineering, Commercial), own problems and their solution end to end, challenge the status quo and help shape how the wider team approaches recurring problems and opportunities.

This is a role for someone who enjoys getting into the detail, thrives on variety, and wants to have a tangible impact on how customers experience Trainline.

In this role as the Senior Data Scientist, you will... 🚄 

- Work across search, supply and commerce, bringing together diverse datasets to tackle complex problems and deliver projects that span multiple pillars.

- Identify opportunities for our customers and our business, using data to shape solutions and building tools and approaches that make the wider team more effective.

- Develop a deep understanding of the customer experience, getting to the root causes of recurring problems (such as conversion declines, checkout errors or searches returning no results) and working cross-functionally to turn insights into lasting improvements.

- Drive continuous improvement by identifying recurring patterns and turning what you learn into reusable tools, frameworks and solutions that reduce investigation time and help the wider team move faster.

- Surface product and commercial opportunities through your analysis, connecting insights to business context and bringing opportunities to the right teams timely to drive action.

- Mentor and guide colleagues across Data and partner teams, helping others build their analytical capability and confidence.

- Partner closely with data scientists, data analysts and cross-functional teams across search, supply, commerce to solve problems that cut across organisational boundaries.

- Navigate competing priorities across multiple areas of the business, bringing structure, clarity and sound judgement to fast-moving and ambiguous situations.

We'd love to hear from you if you have... 🔎 

- Substantial experience as a Data Scientist at a senior level, with the confidence, judgement and autonomy that come from having operated at this level before.

- Track record of owning a business or functional area end to end, taking responsibility for identifying opportunities, shaping the analytical approach and driving outcomes - not just delivering analysis.

- Experience working across multiple business areas or domains, navigating competing priorities and adapting your approach to different problems, stakeholders and contexts.

- A strong track record of delivering measurable business impact through product analytics, translating data and insights into decisions and actions that improve customer and business outcomes.

- Strong SQL and Python skills, used confidently to explore, analyse and draw actionable insights from complex datasets, alongside good engineering practices such as version control and effective use of AI tools to work more efficiently.

- Confidence working with large, unfamiliar and diverse datasets, bringing together multiple data sources to build a robust and comprehensive understanding of a problem.

- Experience mentoring and supporting other Data Scientists, helping colleagues develop their technical skills, analytical thinking and approach to problem-solving.

- Ideally, experience in a technology-driven, digital or marketplace business, although this is not essential.

More information: 

Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits. 

We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one! 

We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy.

Our values represent the things that matter most to us and what we live and breathe everyday, in everything we do: 

- 💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail 

- ✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey 

- 🤝 Travel Together - We're one team 

- ♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact 

We know that having a diverse team makes us better and helps us succeed. And we mean all forms of diversity - gender, ethnicity, sexuality, disability, nationality and diversity of thought. That's why we're committed to creating inclusive places to work, where everyone belongs and differences are valued and celebrated.

Interested in finding out more about what it's like to work at Trainline? Why not check us out on LinkedIn , Instagram and Glassdoor !

title: Product Frontend Engineer
description:
quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app. 

quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end.

Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll.

The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters. 

Where this is going 

Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either.

That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience.

One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy.

Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled. 

Why this role exists 

Today , quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with.

What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards.

That is the opening. 

How we work 

We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing.

We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way.

And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high.

Tasks

What you will own 

Everything on the screen:

- The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account.

- The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components.

- The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device.

- Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native.

- The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished.

Where design ends, engineering begins. 

We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you.

Requirements

Who we are looking for 

You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed.

You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building.

You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels.

You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does.

Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works.

The Team 

We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action.

This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally.

title: Product Engineer, Shop
description:
ABOUT INSIFY 

We sell a mix of insurance products to small businesses (SME's) in the Netherlands, Germany and France, and we are in the process of scaling into more markets. 

Insurance infrastructure is brutal to get right. Every carrier has its own spec, every product its own underwriting rules, every country its own regulatory requirements. Most insurers throw people and process at that complexity - one-off integrations, workarounds on workarounds. We're building it differently: our insurance platform is where we consolidate that complexity, so that launching a new product or market becomes a configuration exercise rather than a rebuild.

Insify is a high-growth scale-up backed by more than €40M from investors like Accel, Munich Re Ventures, and Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg. In five years we've expanded from the Netherlands into France and Germany. Our mission: become the European leader in AI-powered SME insurance.

About the role 

You would join the Shop team, responsible for everything that happens after a small business buys a policy from us. You would help shape how the platform handles the next product and the next country, on a system already carrying live policies and real customers.

The team owns end-to-end policy lifecycle management (mid-term adjustments, automated renewals, cancellations, and payment flows) alongside the backoffice tooling that gives our operations and support teams full visibility and control. We work closely with the Claims Team, and with the Activation Teams that turn a lead into a paying customer. Product and engineering together are 30+ people.

Every country has its own regulatory quirks, and every insurance product has unique data structures, lifecycle rules, and money flows.

As we expand across Europe, our goal isn't to write custom glue code for every new launch. It's to design elegant, reusable platform abstractions. We're building a system where introducing a new country or product feels like snapping modular building blocks together.

You're joining at an exciting inflection point: we have real traction, proven scale, and you get to directly build the foundational platform that powers our next wave of European growth.

What you'll be doing 

- Owning end-to-end the discovery and delivery of crucial platform features that enable our ability to scale as an insurance business

- Continuously and relentlessly seeking opportunities to turn new product demands into platform capabilities and features that scale across countries and insurance product lines

- Challenging our ideas and bringing your own. We encourage each other to act this way, so you can expect the same from others

What you'll need 

- 3+ years building complex web applications and services, with real production ownership

- Ownership & impact instinct - when needed you go beyond your direct stack to get to results, be that data / backend / frontend

- You get real leverage out of AI in your daily work, and you can say where it helped, and where it hurt

- Strong fundamentals in domain-driven design & service oriented architecture

Not all of the above are hard requirements. If you're strong on most of these and eager to grow into the rest, we'd still love to hear from you.

Nice to have 

- Experience building B2B products, especially in insurance & fintech

- Experience working on a product distributed across different country markets

- Strong observability instincts. You know where things will break, and can help others learn that too

Our stack 

TypeScript across the board, running on AWS (IaaC), in a single monorepo. If you have not worked with all of it, that is fine. We care more about how you reason about systems than about which tools you have used before.

We offer 

- Competitive compensation that reflects responsibility and impact. For this role the range is €65,000 to €85,000.

- Trust and autonomy. You'll have real ownership, room to make decisions, and space to shape your role as Insify evolves.

- Hybrid working. 3 days in the office, 2 from home, up to 4 weeks a year working from abroad, and 25 holiday days.

- Pension. We contribute 6% for you.

- Alleo budget. €50 net a month to spend on whatever you want, from the gym to takeaway. It rolls over if you don't use it.

- Learning and coaching. Internal leadership programs, and coaching to go with them.

- A central Amsterdam office. Shared lunches, dogs, whiteboards, and Friday drinks.

- Hardware & setup. A high-spec MacBook Pro, high-res monitors at the office, and comfortable ergonomic seating.

title: Senior C++ Software Engineer
description:
Senior C++ Software Engineer 

Remote (UK-based) | Full-Time 

About Us 

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year ( Risk.net ). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 60+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role 

We're looking for a Senior C++ Software Engineer who can shape the technical direction of our Switchboard trading platform while continuing to write excellent code. You'll work on the most performance-critical components — pricing engines, connectivity gateways, market-data systems, and the messaging layer that ties them together — and you'll have a direct influence on architectural decisions that affect the entire platform.

This is not a role where you write code and throw it over a wall. You build it, you test it, you deploy it, you support it in production, and you improve it. Our engineers own the full lifecycle — from design through to operational excellence. When something breaks at 4pm on a Friday, you're part of the team that investigates and fixes it.

Beyond your own delivery, you'll provide technical oversight across the team — reviewing designs, challenging assumptions, and mentoring engineers who are earlier in their careers. You'll help us maintain the quality bar that our clients depend on, and you'll contribute to the architectural decisions that determine how well our platform scales.

Occasional hours outside the normal working day are required for production releases, scheduled maintenance windows, and Level 3 support during critical incidents. We keep this to a minimum and recognise the commitment — but owning a production trading platform means being there when it matters.

What You'll Work On 

- Modern C++20 and Go on Linux — a modern software stack based on open source

- Cloud-native infrastructure on AWS with colocation in key data centres

- Microsecond-level latency optimisation and high-throughput messaging

- Market-data and reference-data pipelines across multiple asset classes

- FIX protocol integrations with global banks and liquidity providers

- Observability and monitoring — dashboards, alerting, and metrics that make system behaviour visible

- Production systems that handle real money — reliability is not optional

- Architectural oversight — solution design, peer reviews, and technical direction for platform components

- Mentorship — helping junior and mid-level engineers develop their skills, improve their code, and grow into stronger contributors

What We Need 

Technical: 

- Strong C++ with Linux systems programming (5+ years)

- Comfortable working close to the metal — you understand what's underneath your code

- Proven track record of optimising complex, latency-sensitive systems — you can profile, diagnose, and fix performance problems methodically

- Deep understanding of distributed systems architecture and network protocols (TCP/UDP, socket programming, FIX)

- Experience with system design and architectural trade-offs — you've made decisions that stuck and lived with the consequences

- Go experience is a strong bonus — we use Go extensively for microservices and command-line tooling, and you'll be expected to work with it internally. If you don't know it yet, strong C++ engineers pick it up quickly

- Python for scripting, automation, testing, and data analysis — used across the platform for tooling and operational workflows

- Git and shell scripting

- Experience in financial services or trading technology is a plus but not essential

How you work: 

- You ship. You're delivery-focused — you iterate, you improve, you get things into production

- You own it. When you build something, you take responsibility for its behaviour in production. You respond to incidents (15-minute acknowledgement SLA during working hours), investigate issues, and close the loop

- You raise the bar. You conduct thoughtful peer reviews, challenge designs constructively, and hold the team to high standards without slowing it down

- You mentor. You invest in the engineers around you — sharing knowledge, pairing on hard problems, and helping people grow. You make the team better, not just the code

- You write things down. Documentation is not an afterthought — it's how we scale knowledge across a distributed team. If it's not written down, it doesn't exist

- You communicate. We're a distributed team across multiple time zones. Clear, proactive communication — especially when things go wrong — is essential

- You care about quality. You write clean, testable code. You review your peers' work thoughtfully. You push for continuous improvement without gold-plating

- You embrace AI tooling. We use AI tools (Claude, Gemini) to amplify our engineering capability — from code review and debugging to incident investigation and documentation. You don't need to be an expert, but you should be curious and willing to learn

What You Get 

- Real problems — trading systems where performance is measured in microseconds, not user clicks

- Technical influence — direct input into architectural decisions, solution design, and the technical direction of the platform

- An excellent team — senior engineers who care about craft, collaborate openly, and hold each other to high standards

- Ownership — small teams, clear accountability, direct impact on the platform and our clients

- Competitive package — up to 30 days leave + bank holidays, private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites

- Remote-friendly — work from home with flexibility. We trust our people to deliver

- Sustainable pace — we work hard, but we don't burn people out. Balance is how we stay sharp

- Growth — career progression to lead roles, performance specialisation, or technical leadership. We invest in people who invest in us

We believe in transparency, honest feedback, and writing things down. We celebrate delivery, not activity. We frame AI as empowering people — removing toil, amplifying capability, enabling higher-value work.

We aim to build systems that don't depend on the heroics of individuals to maintain and support — systems and processes that are resilient, documented, and sustainable.

Our Hiring Process 

We keep our process focused and respectful of your time. Our process follows three stages.

Stage 1: Initial Conversation with Talent Acquisition
Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes

Stage 2: Hiring Manager Conversation with the relevant team lead or hiring manager
Format: Video call, ~60 minutes

Stage 3: Technical Interview with two members of the relevant engineering team
Format: Video call, interactive session, ~60 minutes

What to expect in each stage will be explained by Talent Acquisition if you're invited to interview. Throughout the process, we aim to keep momentum with no unnecessary delays between stages, and feedback typically comes within a few business days.

*Please note that depending on availability, Stage 2 and 3 may swap around.

How to Apply 

Please apply directly via this job posting — all applications, including those submitted via LinkedIn, are managed through our applicant tracking system, so you'll always land in the same place regardless of where you found this role.

Right to Work: Candidates must have the existing right to work in the UK. We are not currently able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Equal Opportunities: Reactive Markets is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

Reasonable Adjustments: If you need any adjustments or support during the application or interview process, please let us know — we're happy to accommodate.

Data Protection: By applying, you consent to Reactive Markets processing your personal data for recruitment purposes, in line with our privacy policy .
