title: Senior Applied AI Engineer, Document Intelligence
description:
Headquarters: New Jersey, USA

URL: https://vertican.com 

About the role

For 40 years Vertican has buildt software that runs law firms. One year ago we created a new modern AI platform for document automation (processing/extraction/redacting) which our customers have been adopting faster than any product we've ever had. Our suite of AI-enabled products save customers thousands of hours each week by processing high volumes of documents with precision and speed.The AI team is growing and we'd like you to join.

We are hiring an engineer to own the document processing pipelines end to end: design, benchmarking, experimenting with new architectures and tools, threshold required for deploying a new pipeline, etc.

We believe it's important to build our own tooling to help us run, improve, and measure our applications. Therefore, the ideal candidate thinks outside the box on how to not just build the product/pipeline, but also the tooling needed around it.

You will be the first dedicated ML hire on the product taking over from the engineering manager who build the current solution and will work directly with the founding engineering team.

This is a senior, hands-on individual-contributor role, but we are small team and you'll be involved in design, planning, roadmapping, and architectural decisions.

What you will do

Design the pipelines. Own the architecture of the extraction-to-posting pipelines: page classification, field extraction, candidate retrieval, claim matching, confidence gating and the hand-off to human review, etc. Decide where rules end and models begin, and what each stage must guarantee to the next, what the separation of concerns are, etc.

We have different pipelines for different document types and expect that at any given point in time we may have new ones emerge and may consolidate others.

Evaluate new systems before we adopt them. Run structured trials of candidate components and recommend what to keep. Examples include probabilistic record linkage (Splink), Azure AI Content Understanding and Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI and Foundry-hosted models, and LLM agents with tools. Similarly, test new models with the existing pipeline as they are relased from the frontier labs.

Build the evaluation process. You'll own the process of evaluating false positives, false negatives, errors of ommission, etc, that we ultimately use to determine if we should upgrade the pipeline. 

Ship and operate. Take components from trial to production in our python workers on the cloud, instrument them, watch cost and quota, and diagnose the cases reviewers send back.

Set direction. Work with leadereship on the planing for accuracy, cost improvement, and overall product improvements.

What we are looking for

Required 

- 6+ years building ML or data-intensive systems, at least 3 of them owning a production pipeline whose output people acted on.

- Solid backend engineering understanding and ideally cloud architecture understanding.

- Ideally hands-on experience with document understanding: OCR or layout models, field extraction from scanned PDFs, or intelligent document processing products.

- Experience with entity resolution or record linkage at scale (Splink, Dedupe, Zingg, or your own blocking-and-scoring system) against databases of hundreds of thousands of rows.

- You have designed an evaluation from scratch: built a labeled ground-truth set, chosen the metrics, and defended a threshold to a non-technical stakeholder.

- Production experience with LLM APIs, including structured output, tool calling and cost or rate-limit management; you can say when an LLM is the wrong tool.

- Strong Python and SQL. Comfortable reading Postgres query plans and writing the raw query when the ORM gets in the way.

- Engineering/Scientist mindset: you are scientific about testing the pipeline and how results are interpeted/presented.

Nice to have 

- Azure AI services (Content Understanding, Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI, Foundry) or the AWS and GCP equivalents.

- Financial document processing: checks, remittance advices, lockbox files, payment matching, or accounts receivable automation.

- Exposure to collections, legal operations or other regulated workflows handling PII.

- Probabilistic matching theory (Fellegi-Sunter) or active-learning labeling workflows.

- Experience building human-review tooling or feedback loops that feed back into training and evaluation data.

How we work and what we offer

Small team, direct access to large datasets, weekly planning, daily standup, everyone remote in US timezones.

What we offer:

- A small team of tight-knit, like-minded people passionate about high quality software

- Competitive compensation, commensurate with a senior individual-contributor role.

- Monthly payments in USD

Vertican is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on merit and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/vertican-senior-applied-ai-engineer-document-intelligence

title: Software Engineer, Data Integration
description:
Software Engineer, Data Integration

In Brief 

- 
We're a rapidly growing startup on a mission to make healthcare proactive by empowering physicians, nurses, and care team members with real-time data to save lives.

- 
Join us in transforming healthcare from reactive to proactive. You’ll spearhead the engineering effort to build the bridge between massive, complex Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems and the Bayesian platform, delivering critical, real-time insights to help clinicians save lives.

Who We Are 

Bayesian Health’s mission is to improve patient outcomes by empowering clinicians with the insights they need to make the right decision for the right patient at the point-of-care. We’re a diverse team of clinicians, engineers, machine learning experts, product designers, and performance improvement leaders committed to enabling smarter, patient-specific care delivery through unlocking the power of data.

We’re funded by top tier tech and biotech investors: Obvious Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, American Medical Association’s venture arm, Catalio Partners, and LifeForce Capital. Our company has won many awards; most recent recognitions include: Forbes AI Top 50, World Economic Forum Tech Pioneer, Time Best Inventions, BioTech AI Company of the Year.

Read more about our recent publication in Nature Medicine that associates our products with lives saved. 

What you’ll do 

You will be at the forefront of a high-impact engineering mission, building the bridge between massive, complex Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems and the Bayesian platform to generate real-time lifesaving clinical insights that clinicians rely on. Working directly with our health system clients' technical teams, you'll turn fragmented data into immediate, actionable clinical insights that empower care teams to make the best decisions for their patients.

Each integration is a partnership. An Implementation Lead owns the client relationship and project management; a Clinical Integration owns clinical workflow design and training. You own the technical workstream — which means you're the engineer in the room. When a lab result isn't reaching the Bayesian platform for a patient, you have thirty minutes and the client's full attention to trace it from the inbound HL7 message through parsing, mapping, and ingestion, and tell them what happened.

Responsibilities 

- 
Data Integration & Ingestion: Partner with the client's technical teams to design and implement the data integration interface and ingestion pipelines that feed the Bayesian platform with real-time clinical data, powering insights that improve patient outcomes.

- 
Integration Testing & Troubleshooting: Implement automated integration tests at the data layer, and work directly with client technical teams during integration testing to investigate and resolve issues, ensuring smooth and timely integrations.

- 
Production Deployment & Go-Live: Execute the deployment process in close collaboration with the client's technical team, ensuring build and configuration for the data interface, ingestion, and mapping are successfully promoted to production for a seamless launch. During go-live week, you will serve as the technical point of contact for any data integration issues, both internally and with the client's teams, providing clear status updates to cross-functional partners so they can effectively manage client communication.

- 
Integration Tooling & Automation: Develop frameworks and tooling, leveraging LLMs and automation, to increase the efficiency and velocity of our platform integrations as we scale.

- 
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work alongside an Implementation Lead, Clinical Integration, and the client's technical teams to align the data integration workstream with the overall integration effort.

Minimum qualifications 

- 
BS in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience

- 
3+ years building and deploying data pipelines to production, including integration with external APIs (Python preferred)

- 
Strong ability to investigate and resolve data correctness problem end-to-end, across services, storage, and external data sources.

- 
Experience with cloud solutions (AWS, Azure, etc.) and relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, etc.) in a production environment

- 
Experience writing automated integration tests for production systems

- 
Strong communicator with a demonstrated ability to collaborate across functions, working effectively with internal stakeholders, including Project/Product Managers, to align on priorities and deliver results.

Preferred qualifications 

- 
Experience with health data, integration with Electronic Health Records (EHR) systems, and Health IT interoperability standards such as HL7v2 and FHIR.

- 
Experience rolling out production deployments, supporting systems through go-live via an on-call or support rotation, and triaging production issues

- 
Experience working with enterprise customers, and the agility and responsiveness they require.

- 
Experience building internal tooling or automation, including leveraging LLMs, to improve engineering velocity

title: Business Systems Engineer
description:
At ClickUp, we're building the future of work: the first truly converged AI workspace unifying tasks, docs, chat, calendar, and enterprise search, all supercharged by context-driven AI. We are an AI-native company. Every team member is expected to leverage AI daily, and we evaluate AI fluency as part of our hiring process. Join us and help redefine what's possible. 🚀

Job Summary

As a Business Systems Engineer on the GTM Engineering team, you will design, build, and operate the automation and AI systems that power ClickUp's Go-To-Market business — spanning core business products and the integration platforms that connect them. This role is AI-native at its core: you won't just maintain existing workflows, you'll actively advance our GTM systems with intelligent agents, LLM-powered automations, and next-generation integration patterns built on MCP, ClickUp Super Agents, and modern iPaaS tooling.

You'll sit at the intersection of business systems architecture and applied AI — partnering with Sales, Finance, Revenue Operations, and fellow GTM Systems engineers to eliminate toil, accelerate revenue workflows, and build the automated, AI-augmented infrastructure the company runs on. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone deeply fluent in enterprise business systems, excited about deploying production AI, and committed to genuine ownership of the platforms they build — directly supporting GTMSOE's broader mission of operational excellence across the GTM org.

Key Responsibilities

AI-Native Automation & Agent Development

- 
Design and build AI-powered automations and agentic workflows across the GTM tech stack — including Salesforce, NetSuite, Workato, and MuleSoft — to eliminate manual effort and accelerate business operations.

- 
Develop and deploy ClickUp Super Agents and LLM-based automations to automate tasks such as deal data enrichment, quote generation assistance, order validation, revenue recognition triggers, and exception handling in quote-to-cash workflows.

- 
Architect and implement MCP (Model Context Protocol) integrations that allow AI agents to interact with business systems contextually and safely — enabling intelligent, event-driven actions across the GTM platform.

- 
Explore and evaluate emerging AI capabilities (RAG, fine-tuning, multi-agent orchestration) and determine which are production-ready for GTM business systems use cases.

- 
Build reusable AI templates, automation patterns, and agent blueprints that can be extended across the GTM Engineering team.

Business Systems Integration & Architecture

- 
Build and maintain integrations across Salesforce, NetSuite, Workato, MuleSoft, DealHub (CPQ), and other GTM platforms — with a strong bias toward clean architecture, low technical debt, and supportable design.

- 
Own end-to-end integration patterns for critical business flows such as lead-to-opportunity, quote-to-cash, order-to-fulfillment, and revenue reporting pipelines.

- 
Design data flows and transformation logic that keep business data accurate, consistent, and accessible across systems without creating fragile point-to-point dependencies.

- 
Apply a build-vs-buy mindset: evaluate whether a given automation need is best solved with native platform capabilities, iPaaS tooling, or custom code — and make the case clearly.

Platform Development & Tooling

- 
Build internal tooling, low-code/no-code solutions, and lightweight applications using platforms such as Retool, Replit, or similar to extend business systems capabilities with minimal overhead.

- 
Write automation scripts and data transformation logic in Python, JavaScript, or Apex as needed to bridge gaps that platform tooling cannot address natively.

- 
Utilize Zapier, Workato, and similar iPaaS platforms to orchestrate cross-system workflows that are maintainable, observable, and well-documented.

- 
Own the full lifecycle of what you build: discovery, design, development, testing, deployment, documentation, and ongoing optimization.

Reliability, Observability & Continuous Improvement

- 
Monitor the health and performance of automations and integrations you own; proactively identify degradation, data inconsistencies, or failure patterns before they impact business operations.

- 
Conduct root-cause analysis of integration failures or automation breakdowns and drive durable fixes — not just incident patches.

- 
Maintain runbooks and operational documentation so that platform behavior is understandable and recoverable by the broader team.

- 
Gather feedback from business stakeholders and iterate on existing automations to improve accuracy, reduce edge cases, and adapt to evolving GTM processes.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement

- 
Partner with Sales, Revenue Operations, Finance, and Customer Success stakeholders to translate business requirements into well-scoped technical solutions.

- 
Work closely with GTM Systems Engineering, DevOps, and BSA teammates on architecture decisions, intake prioritization, and delivery execution.

- 
Contribute to the GTM Systems Engineering operating model: maintain task hygiene, communicate proactively on large initiatives, and log AI/automation work in the team's AI Excellence registry.

- 
Serve as a subject matter expert for business systems automation and AI — educating stakeholders on what's possible and setting realistic expectations on scope and delivery.

Qualifications

Experience

- 
3–5+ years in a business systems engineering, systems administration, or integration engineering role.

- 
Demonstrated experience building and shipping automations or integrations that delivered measurable business value in production environments.

- 
Hands-on experience with Salesforce and at least one ERP platform (NetSuite strongly preferred).

-

title: Remote Office Assistant
description:
Coalition Technologies is seeking a reliable, detail-oriented, and highly organized Remote Office Assistant to support administrative, bookkeeping, billing, reporting, data entry, and internal operations tasks. This role is ideal for someone with strong communication skills, discretion, attention to detail, and a willingness to learn and grow within a fast-paced remote work environment.

As an Office Assistant, you will help support daily administrative operations, assist with entry-level bookkeeping, organize client documents, support internal reporting, and help maintain accurate company records. This position offers strong growth potential for the right candidate, including opportunities for advancement within the Accounting team or other departments.

We are looking for talented and diligent candidates who perform well on our skills assessments. Strong skills test performance may be considered even if a candidate does not meet every preferred experience or educational background requirement.

Why Join Coalition Technologies? 

Coalition Technologies is committed to delivering high-quality work for our clients while providing our team with a fun, thriving, innovative, and growth-focused work environment. We offer:

- 100% remote work with a company that has supported remote team members for more than a decade

- Competitive profit-sharing bonus plan, with up to 50% of company profits paid to full-time employees each month

- Competitive Paid Time Off plan that supports work-life balance

- Subsidized gym memberships

- Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance packages for eligible US-based team members

- International Health Insurance Reimbursement Program for eligible international team members

- Device upgrade and learning reimbursement programs

- Career development plans with clearly defined goals and rewards

- Additional job-specific incentives and bonuses

Office Assistant Responsibilities 

As an Office Assistant, your duties will include:

- Answering phones and emails

- Completing entry-level bookkeeping tasks, including recording expenses, organizing receipts, and maintaining transaction records

- Resolving billing issues with clients and internal team members

- Providing account access, usage reports, data analysis, and other ad hoc support for team members

- Supporting quality assurance checks for internal and client-facing reports

- Organizing new client contracts, creating invoices, and processing client payments

- Contributing to internal database maintenance, upkeep, and data entry

Required Skills and Qualifications 

The ideal candidate will have:

- Willingness to learn, grow, and collaborate with the team and company as a whole

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills

- High level of discretion, ethics, and trustworthiness

- Strong attention to detail and organizational skills

- Ability to support administrative, bookkeeping, billing, reporting, and data entry tasks

- Innovative thinking and willingness to challenge existing methods when improvement is possible

- Availability to work 40 hours per week, Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Pacific Time

- Reliable remote workspace with a fast computer, quality internet, camera, microphone, and speakers

Preferred Skills 

- The following experience is preferred but not required:

- Intermediate spreadsheet skills

- Experience with bookkeeping or financial record keeping

- Experience with Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel, QuickBooks Online, and Google Workspace

- Experience supporting billing, invoicing, reporting, data entry, or administrative operations

Remote Work Environment 

Coalition Technologies is a fully remote company. Our team works remotely with the support of time tracking software, structured communication, and a company culture designed to help remote team members succeed. We have supported remote team members for more than a decade and welcome qualified applicants from around the world.

Growth Opportunity 

This position offers a strong opportunity for growth. Successful Office Assistants at Coalition Technologies have advanced quickly and earned promotions within the Accounting team and across other departments.

Compensation

For candidates outside of California, New York, Washington, and Colorado, compensation may fall outside the listed range.

title: IT Helpdesk Specialist
description:
WHO WE ARE 🌍

Creating content that resonates is great — turning that attention into growth is even better. That's what Manychat does.

Our AI-powered automations help creators and brands engage with audiences across Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp, and TikTok — at the right moment, with the right message, minus the manual work.

We're 400+ people across three continents behind the leading platform for conversational growth, with AI skills shaping how we build, how we work, and how we grow.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR 🌟 

Are you always one step ahead? The kind of person who has the new hire’s laptop ready before they arrive, notices the meeting-room camera is offline before the call starts, and, after fixing the same problem twice, makes sure nobody has to ask a third time?

We’re looking for an IT Helpdesk Specialist for our Amsterdam office. You’ll own on-site IT here and support colleagues in other hubs remotely, as part of a small global IT team across Amsterdam, Barcelona, São Paulo, Austin, and Yerevan. Our own AI helpdesk agent already answers routine questions in Slack, so your time goes to the work that needs a person: hands-on help, judgment on unclear or risky requests, and care for the people you support.

Our team is organized by domains, and you’ll grow into one of them: Access & Identity (Okta), the area behind most of our requests. Real ownership, from day one. Ready to make it yours?

YOUR FUTURE TEAMMATES 👋 

Meet the IT team: 

We're a small global team in Amsterdam, Barcelona, São Paulo, Austin, and Yerevan, and we keep 400+ manychatters working smoothly and securely. We're organized by domains, so everyone owns an area end to end. AI is part of how we work, including our own helpdesk agent. Our docs live in GitHub, so one good answer helps many people.

WHAT YOU'LL DO 🚀 

On-site and remote support 

- Be the first person colleagues in Amsterdam reach for IT help: at your desk, in Slack, and through our service desk (Freshservice). Support colleagues in other hubs remotely.

- Troubleshoot hardware, software, and connectivity on a Mac-first fleet managed with Jamf, with some Windows devices. Escalate complex issues to IT Administrators with full context, logs, and what you've already tried.

- Get every new hire ready on day one (laptop, peripherals, accounts, and a walkthrough of our tools), and close access and collect equipment for leavers, working with the People and Talent teams.

Office, meeting rooms, and events 

- Keep office IT running: Wi-Fi and wired network (UniFi), printers, office access control, Zoom Rooms, displays, and room schedulers. Make sure meeting rooms are ready every day, and work with the building operator, ISPs, and vendors until every issue is resolved.

- Set up and run AV for All-Hands, internal events, and meetups: microphones, cameras, displays, and streaming when needed. Some events happen outside regular hours.

- Keep the office hardware inventory accurate in Freshservice Assets, manage the loaner pool and spares, and support local purchases, refreshes, and decommissioning.

Access & Identity (Okta) 

- Run day-to-day Okta administration: users, groups and group rules, app assignments, password resets, MFA, and lifecycle states.

- Keep our role-based access model clean, and connect new apps to Okta (SAML or OIDC single sign-on, SCIM provisioning) together with system owners and Security.

- Check every access request for legitimacy and least privilege, and make sure access is right for every joiner, mover, and leaver, including contractors and partners.

- Act as the European backup for this domain, covering access work during European hours, and grow into co-owning it.

Knowledge and automation 

- Write and maintain knowledge base articles in Markdown. Our docs live in GitHub and go through pull requests, and our helpdesk agent answers from them, so one good article saves many tickets.

- Spot repeated requests and fix the cause with a better intake form, an article, or a small automation (Freshservice workflows, n8n, scripts). Use AI tools to research, draft, and script, and check the result before it reaches users.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE 🎯 

- By day 30: you know the office, the stack, and the people. You close tickets end to end and run onboardings on your own.

- By day 60: you add or fix knowledge base articles every week, own meeting rooms and event AV in Amsterdam, and handle routine Okta changes on your own.

- By day 90: you can cover Access & Identity when its owner is away, and you've shipped at least one improvement that removes a recurring type of ticket.

TO SHINE IN THIS ROLE 💥 

You'll need: 

- 3+ years of IT support in a SaaS or cloud-first company, where you've covered a broad scope and know the full helpdesk lifecycle.

- Strong macOS skills and hands-on Jamf (or similar MDM) experience; working knowledge of Windows.

- Hands-on Okta administration (or a comparable identity provider such as Entra ID): groups and group rules, app assignments, SAML or OIDC app integration, SCIM provisioning, and user lifecycle.

- Onboarding and offboarding experience: you know what "day-1 ready" means and deliver it every time.

- Meeting room and event AV experience with Zoom Rooms or similar systems, cameras, microphones, and displays, including setting up an event space or a new office together with integrators and vendors.

- Networking basics: Wi-Fi diagnostics, switching, DHCP, and DNS, enough to find the problem and talk to the vendor.

- Google Workspace admin basics and experience with a service desk tool (Freshservice, Jira Service Management, Zendesk, or similar).

- AI as part of how you work. You use tools like Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini every day, and describe the task clearly, check the output before you trust it. This one's a must.

- Clear writing and fluent English: short, useful answers for users, and articles a colleague can follow without asking you.

- You notice when a request looks wrong (say, an urgent password reset for an executive), know when to stop and escalate, and stay friendly and focused on busy days.

- You fix the cause, not only the ticket: if something happens twice, you find out why and make it stop. You pick up new tools without waiting for training.

- Availability to work from our Amsterdam office 4–5 days a week, with occasional after-hours support for events or planned changes.

It would be great if you have: 

- An Okta certification (Certified Professional or Administrator) or experience with Okta Workflows.

- Freshservice administration experience: workflows, catalog items, SLA policies, and reporting.

- Light scripting or automation skills (Python, bash, n8n, or similar), or a real automation you built yourself, with or without AI help.

- Git and GitHub basics: branches, pull requests, Markdown.

- Experience with Q-SYS or similar audio processing, Logitech room systems, and Zoom Rooms administration.

- Live streaming experience for meetups: multi-camera switching (ATEM, OBS, or similar), audio mixing, and streaming to YouTube.

- UniFi networking and UniFi Access.

- A bit of Microsoft Intune for Windows devices.

WHAT WE OFFER 🤗 

We care deeply about your growth, well-being, and comfort: 

- 💙 Comprehensive health insurance for both you and your family.

- 📚 Professional development budget for conference tickets, online courses, and other relevant resources to help you grow.

- 🫶 Flexible benefits package: no one-size-fits-all perks here. You get a budget and you decide where it goes, from health and wellbeing to family and setting up your home office.

- 🪴 Hybrid work and generous, flexible time off — planned with your team, not rationed by a rigid quota.

- 🍽️ In-office perks, including free meals and snacks.

- 🤝 Company-funded sport activities, annual offsites and team-building events.

- 🤖 AI isn't a perk here — it's how we work. Claude, OpenAI, and more are on by default from day one, and we back teams in adopting whatever makes them faster.

We do not discriminate against qualified employees or applicants because of race, color, religion, gender identity, sex, sexual preference, sexual identity, pregnancy, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, marital status, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, military status, or any other characteristic protected by local law or ordinance. 

This commitment is also reflected through our candidate experience. If you have individual needs that may require an accommodation during the interview process, please indicate this in your application. We will do our best to provide assistance throughout your interview process to ensure you’re set up for success.

title: AI Tooling Engineer
description:
On this journey for over 12 years, Qventus is leading the transformation of healthcare. We enable hospitals to focus on what matters most: patient care. Our innovative solutions harness the power of machine learning, generative AI, and behavioral science to deliver exceptional outcomes and empower care teams to anticipate and resolve issues before they arise.

Our success in rapid scale across the globe is backed by some of the world's leading investors. At Qventus, you will have the opportunity to work with an exceptional, mission-driven team across the globe, and the ability to directly impact the lives of patients. We’re inspired to work with healthcare leaders on our founding vision and unlock world-class medicine through world-class operations. #LI-MB1

About the Role 

We're hiring Engineers dedicated to building AI-powered tools that change how work gets done inside the company. You'll embed with teams across operations, customer success, and finance, find the work that's slow and manual, and ship AI agents and automations that actually get adopted.

This is a build-fast, talk-to-humans, own-the-problem role - not a research role and not a pure-infrastructure role. You'll define what "internal AI" looks like here from scratch.

Who this is for 

You're energized by ambiguity and ownership. You'd rather ship a rough tool this week, watch someone use it, and improve it than spend a month on a perfect spec. You like sitting with a non-technical teammate, understanding their actual workflow, and turning it into something that saves them hours. You're comfortable being the only person who owns a problem end to end.

Who you will work with 

- You'll partner closely with the CEO and founders on identifying the highest-leverage operational problems to solve and shaping where internal AI goes next. This is a rare amount of executive access to an engineering role. 

- You’ll work alongside functional leaders across the business to understand their priorities, surface opportunities , and align on what to build. Your work will be visible and leadership level from day one. 

- Operations, Customer Success, Finance, People/Talent Acquisition, Engineering, IT and Data teams, these are your internal customers and collaborators. You'll embed with them, and learn their workflows and ship tools they actually use. 

What you'll actually build 

Examples of the kind of work waiting for you:

- An agent that drafts customer success replies from our knowledge base and ticket history

- A Slack-based workflow that routes and pre-fills finance approvals

- An internal eval harness so we can trust the LLM features we ship

- A tool that lets the ops team query [internal system] in plain language

You won't do all of these at once — you'll pick the highest-impact one, ship it, and move to the next.

What we're looking for 

- 1–3 years building software — backend services, internal tools, automations, or API-driven apps. Internships and co-ops count.

- Strong in TypeScript and/or Python .

- You've built something with LLMs — an agent, a RAG pipeline, a copilot, a prompt-driven tool — through work, a side project, or coursework. We care that you've shipped, not where.

- Comfortable wiring systems together: APIs, webhooks, SaaS integrations, async workflows.

- You can talk to non-technical stakeholders, figure out what they really need, and drive adoption — this matters as much as the code.

- You move fast under ambiguity and iterate from real feedback.

Bonus, not required 

- Built copilots, agents, or workflow automations before

- Used an orchestration framework (LangChain, Temporal, or similar)

- Worked with vector databases or retrieval systems

- Integrated with Salesforce, Slack, Zendesk, Notion, or Jira

- Startup / high-growth experience

What success looks like 

- First few weeks: shipped your first internal tool and it's in active daily use by a business team.

- Within 2 months: 2–3 tools live, and stakeholders are coming to you with ideas.

- By month 3: you've set the team's baseline practices for evals, prompt management, and safe LLM deployment — the foundation the function grows on.

Compensation for this role is based on market data and takes into account a variety of factors, including location, skills, qualifications, and prior relevant experience. Salary is just one part of the total rewards package at Qventus. We also offer a range of benefits and perks, including Open Paid Time Off, paid parental leave, professional development, wellness and technology stipends, a generous employee referral bonus, and employee stock option awards.

Salary Range

$120,000—$150,000 USD

title: AI Developer
description:
Salvo Software is a global technology company specializing in custom software development and advanced engineering solutions. With distributed teams across the US, LATAM, and India, we partner with clients to build high-performance, scalable systems that solve complex technical challenges. Our culture values innovation, ownership, and engineering excellence. We're growing our AI department and are looking for a hands-on AI Developer to help build it.

Role Overview We are looking for an AI Developer to join and strengthen our AI department. Your core work will be building and operating LLM-powered systems: serving open-source models with Ollama and llama.cpp, building RAG pipelines, and developing MCP integrations that connect large language models to real tools and data. Solid DevOps fundamentals - Docker, CI/CD, Azure - support this work, but AI engineering is the heart of the role.

You don't need to be a deep ML researcher. What matters is production-grade Python, strong fundamentals, and the aptitude to learn fast. You'll work closely with our engineering and product teams to take LLM-powered features from prototype to reliably deployed systems, with mentorship available as you ramp up in areas like RAG architecture, Kafka, and advanced MCP work.

Key Responsibilities AI / LLM Engineering (core focus)

- Serve and operate open-source LLMs using Ollama and llama.cpp, locally and in on-prem environments.
- Build and maintain RAG pipelines: embeddings, vector databases, chunking strategies, and retrieval quality.
- Develop MCP (Model Context Protocol) integrations connecting LLMs to internal tools and data sources.
- Build backend services in Python that power ML inference and AI-driven product features.
- Parse and process structured and semi-structured data (XML/XSD, Office document formats) as pipeline inputs.
- Grow into model optimization over time: quantization (GGUF), GPU/CUDA tuning, and offline/air-gapped deployments.
DevOps & Infrastructure (supporting)

- Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for AI services (Azure DevOps preferred; GitHub Actions / GitLab CI also used).
- Deploy AI workloads to Microsoft Azure,AWS and containerize services with Docker.
- Automate operational tasks with Python, Bash and/or PowerShell scripting.
- Troubleshoot across the stack - dig into root causes rather than patching symptoms.
- Support event-driven architectures using Apache Kafka (producers/consumers).

- 3â5+ years engineering experience with production-level Python for building real services, LLM inference, RAG pipelines, and automated tooling.
- Hands-on LLM & AI integration serving models via Ollama/llama.cpp, implementing vector retrieval/RAG, and developing MCP integrations (GPU/CUDA tuning & model quantization nice to have).
- Cloud & Infrastructure expertise covering Azure/AWS deployments, Docker containerization, Linux/Windows admin, and CI/CD automation (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, or GitLab CI), with Terraform, Kubernetes, Kafka, or systems languages (Go, Rust, C++) as a plus.
- DevOps, Security & Operations awareness, including Git workflows, scripting (Python, Bash, PowerShell), observability tools (Prometheus/Grafana), DevSecOps, and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, Zero Trust).
- Strong problem-solving & communication with a root-cause troubleshooting mindset, self-directed learning, strong ownership, and seamless remote/distributed team collaboration.

title: DevOps Engineering Intern
description:
About Sonio

Each year, 140M children are born. Birth defects affect 1 in 33 births in developed countries, and in 50% of cases, they are not detected during prenatal examinations. Prenatal medicine is particularly complex, and the scans impose heavy responsibilities on healthcare professionals. They can also be a source of stress for future parents.

Resulting from 5 years of collaboration between world-renowned experts from Necker Hospital and Ecole Polytechnique, Sonio uses artificial intelligence to improve prenatal screening and diagnosis. Based on patented algorithms and a proprietary expert database, Sonio aims to become the reference tool to help practitioners improve screening, reduce diagnostic errors, and optimize pregnant women’s medical path.

Sonio's mission is to improve women's and children's health by promoting access and quality of care through technological innovation, medical expertise, and collective intelligence.

About the role 

We are looking for a DevOps / Platform Engineering intern to join our Platform team (DevOps, Data and Staff Engineers), which runs the infrastructure behind our SaaS platform. As the platform grows, so do our internal operational requests. Your mission will be to find out how far AI agents can take this RUN work off our plate, without giving up control.

Your main mission will be to: 

- Build an AI agent that turns internal infrastructure requests (provisioning a new service, managing AWS resources and access, environment variables or app configuration, Kubernetes or ArgoCD resources) into ready-to-review GitHub Pull Requests:

- Understand. The agent parses the request and picks the matching runbook.

- Generate. It produces the Terraform, Kubernetes or ArgoCD changes in our IaC repositories.

- Validate. It runs automated checks: tests, linting, and security and misconfiguration scans.

- Propose. It opens a traceable Pull Request for human review and approval.

- Design the guardrails that make this safe: least-privilege access, approval steps, and predictable, repeatable runs. The AI never changes production on its own, and engineers stay in control of every change,

- Deliver a working proof of concept on real internal requests, built so it can grow into a production-ready tool.

The AI never changes production on its own. Engineers stay in control, and every change is reviewed, tested and traceable.

Our infrastructure stack 

- Cloud: AWS, multi-region

- Infrastructure as Code: Terraform

- Containers & GitOps: Kubernetes on EKS, Helm, ArgoCD

- CI/CD: GitHub Actions

- Observability: Datadog

- Security & Compliance: vulnerability and misconfiguration scanning, least-privilege IAM, and a HITRUST/SOC2-driven change process

- Backend: Elixir/Phoenix

About the profile 

Sonio is a mission-driven company so interest in our mission is critical. Other requirements are:

- Currently in Master 2 / Bac+5 of Engineering School or University, you are majoring in Computer Science and are looking for an internship lasting between 5 and 6 months,

- Good knowledge of AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes, and Git and CI/CD workflows,

- Solid scripting skills (Python or similar) and a security-minded approach to infrastructure changes,

- Strong interest in AI agents and LLMs applied to real engineering problems,

- Experience with ArgoCD, Helm or Datadog is a plus,

- You speak English and ideally French.

€98.200 — €132.800 EUR

title: Quality Assurance Engineer II
description:
Bloomreach is building the world’s premier agentic platform for personalization .We’re revolutionizing how businesses connect with their customers, building and deploying AI agents to personalize the entire customer journey.

- We're taking autonomous search mainstream, making product discovery more intuitive and conversational for customers, and more profitable for businesses.

- We’re making conversational shopping a reality, connecting every shopper with tailored guidance and product expertise — available on demand, at every touchpoint in their journey.

- We're designing the future of autonomous marketing , taking the work out of workflows, and reclaiming the creative, strategic, and customer-first work marketers were always meant to do.

And we're building all of that on the intelligence of a single AI engine — Loomi — so that personalization isn't only autonomous…it's also consistent.From retail to financial services, hospitality to gaming, businesses use Bloomreach to drive higher growth and lasting loyalty. We power personalization for more than 1,400 global brands, including American Eagle, Sonepar, and Pandora.

Become a Quality Engineer for Bloomreach! 

The Data Pipeline team is a backend-focused engineering team that cares deeply about quality and reliability. We believe in autonomy, we trust data, and we own what we ship end-to-end. We move our customers' data in and out of Bloomreach Engagement reliably and at a high rate:

- Our clients feed their visitors' behavior through real-time tracking to our platform. The data then can be analyzed and used for marketing automation. We process tens of thousands of requests per second .

- Imports are critical for our clients to utilize our platform to the fullest. We import millions of rows of data and continuously improve the throughput and reliability of our imports and integrations with other data storages.

- We are also responsible for exporting data from our platform to Google's BigQuery using Google's DataFlows, PySpark and Apache Beam, allowing data access by our clients.

- We run and support our services in production, handling high-volume traffic using Google Cloud Platform and Kubernetes .

Every one of these flows is something our customers rely on being correct, at scale. That is the terrain your testing and automation will cover.

You won't be doing this alone: you'll join an experienced Senior Quality Engineer already on the team, so you'll have a buddy to ramp up with, bounce ideas off, and share the quality mission with from day one. We work remotely first (from Central & Eastern Europe), but we are more than happy to meet you in our nice offices in Bratislava, Brno or Prague. And if you are interested in who will be your engineering manager, check out Adam's LinkedIn .

Intrigued? Read on 🙂 ...

What challenge awaits you? 

As a Quality Engineer in Data Pipeline, you own quality for systems that move huge volumes of customers' data in real time, at scale, across many integrations. This is a backend, data-heavy world: a tracking API on one side, an internal message format and multiple storages on the other, with Kafka, GCP and Kubernetes in between. Guaranteeing quality here means understanding how data flows end-to-end and where it can go wrong.

We need you to bring engineering rigor to that quality. Concretely, you will:

- Own end-to-end and integration testing. Complex data pipelines can behave correctly component by component yet still surprise you end-to-end. You design the tests that validate real behavior across components, so we can ship changes to high-scale integrations with confidence.

- Build automation that runs repeatedly in CI. Turn testing into automated integration and end-to-end suites (e.g. Robot Framework, API tests) wired into the deployment pipeline, giving engineers fast, reliable feedback on every change.

- Go deep in the imports domain. Imports are a rich, well-defined area with plenty to reason about. You'll build deep context so you can proactively tell the team what to test, how, and why , and where the edge cases hide.

- Shift left. Be part of grooming and design from day one, thinking about test cases and failure modes while features are being shaped rather than after the fact.

- Strengthen the pipeline core too. Beyond imports, help raise quality across the Data Pipeline core as you grow context.

- Partner with the developers. Quality is a shared responsibility: developers own their in-source tests and you add the outside-in automation layer and perspective. You make the whole team better at testing, not the place work gets handed off to.

Your responsibilities 

- Design and own black-box, API-level and integration/end-to-end test automation for Data Pipeline services, primarily in the imports domain.

- Build and maintain automated test suites in CI/CD (GitLab) that gate deployments and catch regressions across components.

- Read Go/Python pipeline code well enough to find holes and design meaningful test cases - you don't need to ship features, you need to understand the system.

- Drive test strategy in grooming and design reviews - test types on the ticket, acceptance criteria, edge cases, failure modes.

- Pair with our current Data Pipeline QA to spread automation and code-adjacent testing practices across the team.

- Use telemetry and reproduction to turn production incidents into durable, automated regression tests.

Our tech stack 

- Languages: Python (primary), Go (enough to read pipeline code)

- Test automation: Robot Framework (API/integration and Browser-based E2E), CI-driven suites in GitLab, with ReportPortal / Allure reporting

- Platform you'll test against: Apache Kafka, Google Cloud Platform, Kubernetes, BigQuery, MongoDB, Redis

- CI/CD & tooling: GitLab, Jira, Confluence

- AI coding agents: Cursor, Claude Code, ...

- ... and much more 🙂

Your qualifications 

Must have 

- You write test automation in code - integration and API tests in CI, in Python / Go or a similar language.

- You can read backend/pipeline code (Go or Python) well enough to find gaps and reason about where a change can break something else. Useful QA sees the cross-component failure the feature author might missed.

- You are comfortable owning black-box, API and integration/end-to-end automation - the outside-in layer. (In-source unit and in-repo integration tests remain with the feature developers.)

- You want to work primarily in code and automation . If you are coming from a mostly manual testing background, that is fine - as long as you are excited to make automation your main craft, because that is where this role lives.

- You are comfortable in grooming and design from day one - a shift-left mindset, defining test types and cases on the ticket before code is written.

- You can learn and adapt - essential when navigating a large codebase and a data domain that mixes tracking, imports, and multiple storages.

- You know how to be effective in a remote-first environment.

- Fluent use of AI coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Gemini CLI, or similar) as part of your daily workflow.

Strongly preferred 

- Prior backend exposure (an internship or role where you wrote code, or worked under a senior who set up proper testing/automation workflows) - it makes the pipeline world far less of a black box.

- Experience with ETL / data-pipeline testing: connectors, ingest at scale, data cleanup and transformations, and validating data landing correctly in target storages.

- Experience testing systems built on Kafka, GCP, or BigQuery.

- Familiarity with test frameworks such as Robot Framework, Playwright or API testing tooling (Postman and beyond).

Personal qualities 

- Ownership - you take quality from detection through to a durable, automated fix that prevents the next regression.

- Systematic thinking - you find root causes, not symptoms, and you document what you learn so the team levels up.

- Collaboration - you make developers better at testing rather than becoming the place work gets "thrown over the wall".

- Curiosity - you enjoy peeling back a data pipeline until you understand what can go wrong and why.

Your success story 

In 30 days 

- Get to know the Data Pipeline team, the company, and the most important processes.

- Set up your local and cloud development environment and complete the Engagement engineering onboarding.

- Understand how our pipelines work end-to-end - tracking, imports, exports - and how we approach testing and automation, with a focus on the imports domain.

In 90 days 

- Deliver your first meaningful quality improvement: an automated integration or end-to-end suite for a real imports flow, wired into CI so it gates deployments.

- Be active in grooming and design reviews, defining test cases and surfacing edge cases and cross-component risks before implementation.

- Pair with our current QA to share automation practices and broaden the team's quality coverage.

In 180 days 

- Own the quality posture of the imports domain end-to-end - the team relies on your suites and your judgment on what "tested" means.

- Drive measurable improvements: more of the pipeline covered by repeatable automated tests, faster feedback in CI, and higher release confidence across the team.

- Extend your coverage and influence into the Data Pipeline core.

- Find out that our values are truly lived by us . We are dreamers and builders . Join us!

title: Senior Software Engineer — AI-Native Engineering (XTM Foundation)
description:
🌀 The Company

Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action. 

Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action.

At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative.

As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future.

🎯 The Role

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer who is genuinely, deeply convinced that AI is transforming the way software gets built, and who wants to make that transformation happen at Filigran.

We are looking for an engineer first. This isn't a "we bought Copilot, please roll it out" role, and it isn't only a tooling or development role either: part of the job is building, part of it is trying things on real work, measuring them and telling teams honestly what works and what doesn't. This is a practitioner role for someone who has already lived this shift, who experiments constantly, who knows what works and what doesn't, and who can bring 60 engineers along on that journey.

You will join the XTM Foundation team as Filigran's internal reference on AI-Native engineering. You'll propose our approach, build our practices, run experiments, and share the results so that teams can change how they work with confidence. You'll be hands-on, opinionated, and always one step ahead.

💼 Your Responsibilities

- 
Define and own Filigran's AI-Native engineering strategy: which tools, which workflows, which practices, and how they evolve as the landscape moves fast.

- 
Run structured experiments to evaluate new AI coding tools and agents (Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Cline, MCP servers, code generation agents…), measure their real impact on velocity and quality, and translate findings into actionable recommendations.

- 
Build the guardrails and engineering standards that ensure AI-generated code is maintainable, tested, and consistent with our quality bar — not just fast to produce.

- 
Work directly with product engineering teams (~80 engineers) to embed AI practices into their day-to-day workflows: pair programming with AI, AI-assisted code review, test generation, documentation, and beyond.

- 
Share what you learn. Run internal talks, workshops, and demos. Be the person engineers come to when they want to understand what's possible, and what isn't. Show real results, including the failures.

- 
Stay permanently ahead of the curve — the AI tooling landscape moves weekly. You'll be the one tracking it, filtering the noise, and surfacing what actually matters for a team like ours.

- 
Work in the XTM Foundation team to turn AI practices into shared building blocks for every product team: agent workflows in our CI pipelines (dependency updates, flaky test triage, review assistance), shared MCP servers and prompt libraries, versioned AI configuration in the repositories, and written rules on tools and data handling that apply to everyone.

- 
Contribute to Filigran's external voice on AI-Native engineering — blog posts, open-source contributions, conference talks — as the opportunity arises.

🤝 Who You'll Work With

- 
Reports to: Principal Engineer of XTM Foundation team.

- 
Key collaborators: Engineers and Engineering Managers across OpenCTI, OpenAEV, and OpenGRC product teams; VP of Technology; CTO.

- 
Working model: You will split your time between XTM Foundation team work (research, experimentation, standards) and direct collaboration with product teams to embed AI practices in real engineering workflows.

🧬 Profile We're Looking For

- 
7+ years of software engineering experience — you are a strong engineer first. You understand what good code looks like, and that's what makes your judgment on AI credible.

- 
You are genuinely AI-first in how you work. Not as a trend, not as a productivity hack. You've already transformed how you build software, you can show what you built and what you measured, and you want to help others do the same.

- 
Proven experience deploying AI-assisted development practices within an engineering team: you've done this before, you know what resistance looks like, and you know what actually works and what doesn't.

- 
Deep, hands-on familiarity with the current AI coding tooling landscape: agentic coding tools, LLM-powered code review, prompt engineering for development workflows, MCP ecosystems, and what's coming next.

- 
Strong full-stack engineering background — you can evaluate AI output across the whole stack and contribute code yourself when it matters.

- 
You can make a clear case, with evidence. You're a natural communicator who can discuss a trade-off with a skeptical senior engineer just as well as you can help a junior developer get started.

- 
Comfortable working in a remote-first, async culture with teams across multiple time zones; clear communicator in English.

- 
Autonomy and ownership mindset: you drive this agenda without waiting for direction, and you bring others with you rather than working alone.

- 
Bonus: experience with open-source communities, cybersecurity domain knowledge, contributions to AI tooling projects, or public writing/speaking on AI-Native engineering.

🌱 Why Join Filigran? More than just a job. 

We are a fast-growing, global and remote-first company , and we believe the best work combines purpose, impact and innovation . You’ll work alongside talented people across the world who care about what they build, how they build it, and the impact they make on the broader cybersecurity ecosystem.

⭐ Be part of something bigger 

We believe we do work that matters. Our open-source approach means that work extends beyond Filigran. You’re contributing to technology and ideas that strengthen a global community of defenders and help make cybersecurity more open and collaborative.

💻 Work at the edge of what’s next 

We bring together cybersecurity, open source and AI — giving you the opportunity to work with emerging technologies, experiment with new ways of working, and contribute to how they are applied in practice.

🌍 Global opportunity without borders

- Experience with database proxies or load-balancing layers (MaxScale, HAProxy, ProxySQL, or similar).

- Experience with PostgreSQL, Vitess, TiDB, ScyllaDB, ClickHouse or internal database platforms; operational knowledge of Kafka, Redis/Valkey or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch.

You’ll be part of the foundational team defining how our Australia engineering office operates. Expect to move fast, own outcomes, and see your work drive real-world impact within weeks, not quarters.

Who You Are

Your work will touch millions of deliveries each month and help define Nash’s engineering footprint across APAC.

title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, Platform
description:
Orbital Industries is an AI Industrial company, with frontier AI embedded at every step in the production of critical physical products - from creating advanced materials to engineering and manufacturing.

Every Orbital Industries product is developed using CurieOS, our AI operating system, uniting AI-automated hardware engineering with AI-designed material science to achieve breakthrough real-world performance. We also offer CurieOS to our customers and partners, extending the same platform and workflows that power Orbital Industries to their own teams and products.

We have an ambitious mission and need excellent people in all our teams - AI research, operations, advanced materials, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering and manufacturing.

Working at Orbital Industries means working in vertically integrated teams across the full stack, from molecules to manufacturing. We're looking for people who have a love of physical technology, curiosity in AI and a desire to learn.

The role 

Physical engineering is one of the hardest domains for AI. Designs have to meet standards, calculations must be deterministic and checkable, and a wrong number can end up in a power system or a data centre. CurieOS is built to let agents do real engineering work and to show exactly how every output was produced.

The platform team builds the foundation that every workflow, agent and product on CurieOS depends on, and runs it in production for people who need to trust it. Your work sets the floor for how reliable our AI is, and the ceiling for what it can do.

This is a small team, and you'll shape what we build as well as how. You'll see the results of those decisions in production within days. If you want a narrow, well-defined slice of a large system, this isn't the role. If you want to own a platform while it scales, it is.

How we work 

We build with agents, not just for them. Everyone on the team works with the latest frontier models and coding agents every day, and token budgets won't hold you back. Part of what we build is CurieOS's ability to work on itself: triaging defects, proposing fixes and opening pull requests for engineers to review. So engineers here spend more of their time on design, review and judgement, and less on typing. If you already work this way, you'll feel at home. If you want to see how far it can go, this is the place to find out.

You'll also work alongside our AI researchers, turning cutting-edge research and evals into things that run in the platform and in production.

What you'll work on first 

In your first six months you'll work across the parts of CurieOS that customers have to be able to trust. Like everyone on the team you'll touch most of them, and go deepest where your interests take you:

- Tenancy, isolation and identity. How CurieOS keeps each customer separate, from shared multi-tenant accounts to dedicated single-tenant deployments. That covers data isolation, SSO and access control. You'll also be an engineering voice in customer security reviews.

- Release and production. How changes get to production safely: release gates, staged rollouts and rollback, automated smoke tests, on-call and incident response. We ship often, and you'll build what lets us keep doing that without breaking what customers rely on.

- Agent quality in production. Measuring how well agents perform on real customer workflows, working with our researchers to bring the latest evals into the platform, and using those measurements to decide what is good enough to release. A model or prompt change should have to pass the same gate as a code change.

- Observability and cost. Knowing the platform is healthy and what it costs. That means SLOs, tracing and alerting, plus cost telemetry and usage metering for every workflow and every customer, so we can see where model and compute spend goes and make deliberate choices about it.

- Infrastructure and deployment. One standard for how CurieOS is deployed, configured and upgraded in each environment, across our own cloud accounts, GPU capacity and customer-dedicated deployments.

Where the platform is going 

Once those foundations are solid, there's a lot to shape next:

- Traceable results. Provenance for every number an agent produces: which inputs, tools, models and versions went into it, so our users can check it and sign it off.

- Agent runtime and context. How agents plan, call tools, manage context across long-running work and hand off to people at the right moment.

- Durable workflows. Orchestration that survives failures, retries and runs lasting hours, mixing agent steps with deterministic calculations.

At Staff level, you'd set technical direction across these areas, not just within one. You'd own one of them end to end, run the design reviews that our research and forward deployed teams build on, make the architecture calls that are hard to reverse, and help shape how we hire and grow engineers.

Our stack 

Python services on Kubernetes, running on AWS plus specialist GPU clouds for heavy compute. Strong engineers from Go, Kotlin, Java or a comparable stack will pick up the language quickly. What matters more is that you've run real systems in the cloud.

You'll have most of these 

- Designed and built backend services that other teams or customers relied on, and made the key decisions yourself.

- Owned a system in production after it shipped: the cloud infrastructure it ran on, on-call, incidents, how changes went out, and the monitoring that told you it was healthy.

- Built and run something where LLMs do real work for real users, and dealt with the cost, latency and quality trade-offs that come with it.

- Used coding agents heavily in your own work, with opinions on where they help and where they break.

- Led a project end to end, made trade-offs you can explain, and raised the bar for the engineers around you.

Bonus points 

- Shipped software to external enterprise customers: SSO, tenant isolation, per-customer deployments, security reviews.

- Run infrastructure as code at scale, or GPU workloads across more than one cloud provider.

- Helped a system or a company through a scaling phase, such as a platform going from internal use to many external customers.

- Worked closely with researchers, scientists, engineers or other domain experts and built what they actually needed.

- For Staff: a track record of setting technical direction beyond your own team, such as architecture other teams adopted, a migration you led across several teams, or engineers you've grown into senior roles.

You don't need a background in materials, chemistry or engineering. You'll pick up the domain from the people who have it.

Why Orbital 

Orbital Industries is an AI Industrial company. We put frontier AI into the making of critical physical products, from advanced materials to data-centre engineering. Our research team works at the cutting edge, from universal interatomic potentials to GPU-native simulation, and we turn that research into tools engineers use every day. CurieOS is the platform that brings it together: the AI operating system the whole company runs on, which customers are starting to depend on for their own engineering work too.

Orbital is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: Développeur Python IA
description:
Développeur Python IA (H/F) 

Paris/Lille | Secteur Assurance 

Pourquoi cette opportunité ? 

Parce que vous participerez à la construction de notre stratégie d’intelligence artificielle, que nous sommes en train de définir.
Vous rejoindrez une équipe motivée et talentueuse, dont la mission est d’intégrer l’IA au cœur de nos processus métier.

L’objectif est de répondre aux besoins de nos équipes comme à ceux de nos clients, et d’automatiser certaines tâches à faible valeur ajoutée.

Éléments clés 

- Concevoir des solutions RAG et agentiques appliquées à des cas d’usage métier concrets.
- Développer et orchestrer des agents tout en assurant la traçabilité des sources et la maîtrise des hallucinations.
- Contribuer directement au workflow de paramétrage produit KELIA, avec une validation humaine intégrée aux étapes clés.
- Participer à la mise en production des assistants, de leur API jusqu’à leur intégration dans l’interface web interne.

Ce qu’il faut savoir : 

Nous recherchons un(e) Développeur Python IA pour rejoindre notre équipe R&D à Paris ou Lille

Vous interviendrez sur l’ensemble du cycle de vie des solutions, de la conception jusqu’à la mise en production, en mobilisant différentes approches : modèles de langage (LLM), apprentissage supervisé, clustering et autres techniques de machine Learning.

Un volet important de la mission concerne également le paramétrage produit : l’objectif est d’extraire les informations pertinentes des conditions générales, de proposer un paramétrage, de prévoir une validation par un expert à chaque étape et de produire un fichier directement importable dans KELIA.

Missions principales : 

Vous développez en Python des fonctionnalités IA.

- Ingestion documentaire : extraire le texte et les tableaux des PDF, des pages Confluence, des documents SharePoint et des dépôts GitLab, puis découper, indexer et mettre à jour ces contenus avec des jobs asynchrones.
- Recherche : recherche hybride (sémantique et mots-clés), filtres par collection et par chemin, reranking, et recherche visuelle sur les pages de documents.
- Agents et LLM : développer des agents avec LangGraph (routage, recherche, filtrage, réflexion, réponse), écrire et versionner les prompts, citer les sources, et répondre « je ne trouve pas » quand l'information manque.
- Workflow de paramétrage produit : contribuer à l'agent qui extrait les informations des conditions générales, propose le paramétrage, fait valider chaque étape par un expert et produit un fichier importable dans KELIA.
- Qualité : maintenir des jeux de tests, mesurer le taux de bonnes réponses, suivre les réponses inventées et vérifier que les résultats sont stables d'un run à l'autre.
- Coût et latence : suivre la consommation de tokens, le temps de première réponse et le cache, et choisir le bon modèle pour chaque tâche.
- API : exposer les assistants en API, avec des réponses en streaming, et les intégrer à l'interface web interne.
- Documenter votre code, écrire des tests et participer aux revues de code.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si: 

- Vous êtes diplômé(e) d’un Bac+5 en informatique ou assurance
- Vous maîtrisez Python 3.11+ et êtes à l’aise avec le développement d’API via FastAPI , Pydantic et le streaming SSE .
- Vous avez une expérience ou un réel intérêt pour les solutions d’ IA générative , les LLM et les architectures agentiques avec LangChain , LangGraph et LiteLLM .
- Vous connaissez les principes de RAG , de recherche hybride, d’embeddings et de reranking, idéalement avec Qdrant .
- Vous savez travailler avec des sources documentaires variées et leur ingestion, notamment des PDF , Confluence , SharePoint ou GitLab , avec des outils tels que Docling .
- Vous êtes à l’aise avec les environnements de stockage et de persistance reposant sur PostgreSQL et le stockage objet S3 .
- Vous accordez de l’importance à l’observabilité et à la qualité des solutions IA, notamment au suivi des prompts, des traces, des logs, des coûts et des performances, avec des outils comme MLflow .
- Vous êtes sensibilisé aux enjeux de sécurité, d’authentification et de gestion des rôles, notamment avec Keycloak .
- Vous évoluez avec aisance dans un environnement d’industrialisation moderne utilisant Git , GitLab CI , Docker , Kubernetes , Helm et pytest , ainsi que des outils collaboratifs comme Jira et Confluence .

Ce que vous apportez 

- Une bonne maîtrise de Python et de ses bonnes pratiques : tests (pytest), typage, gestion des dépendances.
- Votre expérience dans l’utilisation des API de LLM et bases du prompt engineering, y compris les sorties structurées.
- Votre compréhension du fonctionnement d'un RAG : embeddings, découpage, recherche, génération.
- Une bonne maîtrise du SQL et notions de bases de données.
- Git et travail en équipe.

Pourquoi nous joindre: 

- Pour contribuer à une stratégie où l’intelligence artificielle est un levier clé de la feuille de route technologique, avec des solutions intégrées au cœur des outils métiers.
- Pour travailler sur des cas d’usage concrets d’IA générative, de RAG et d’agents LLM, de l’expérimentation jusqu’à l’industrialisation.
- Pour associer des technologies IA de pointe à une expertise métier forte dans le secteur de l’assurance et créer des solutions à impact réel.
- Prêt(e) à démarrer une nouvelle expérience ? 
Envoyez-nous votre candidature et commençons la conversation

title: Data Science Internship
description:
About Sonio

Each year, 140M children are born. Birth defects affect 1 in 33 births in developed countries, and in 50% of cases, they are not detected during prenatal examinations. Prenatal medicine is particularly complex, and the scans impose heavy responsibilities on healthcare professionals. They can also be a source of stress for future parents.

Resulting from 5 years of collaboration between world-renowned experts from Necker Hospital and Ecole Polytechnique, Sonio uses artificial intelligence to improve prenatal screening and diagnosis. Based on patented algorithms and a proprietary expert database, Sonio aims to become the reference tool to help practitioners improve screening, reduce diagnostic errors, and optimize pregnant women’s medical path.

Sonio's mission is to improve women's and children's health by promoting access and quality of care through technological innovation, medical expertise, and collective intelligence.

About the role 

We are looking for a DS/ML Engineer intern to join our Data Science team. Your mission will at the crossing of R&D, ML Engineering and product, supervised by senior ML engineers. You will work on developing of our existing Deep Learning/Computer Vision pipelines using State-of-the-art algorithms.

Your main mission will be to: 

• Develop clinical understanding of fetal ultrasound in the anatomical areas you will work on,
• Explore and train different approaches for Detection and Segmentation of anatomical structures and views, and integrate your results in our ML infrastructure (AWS, SageMaker, MLflow),
• Explore the possibility of training Foundation Models for Ultrasound Imaging,
• Run evaluation protocols consistent with the way our models are evaluated during regulatory submissions, and document your experiments so the team can build on them. Publication is possible and encouraged if the results support it.

About the profile 

Sonio is a mission-driven company so interest in our mission is critical. Other requirements are:

• Currently in Master 2 / Bac+5 of Engineering School or University, you are majoring in Computer Science or Data Science and are looking for an internship lasting between 5 and 6 months,
• Good knowledge of Machine Learning and Deep Learning algorithms, and the willingness to explore and work on state-of-the-art algorithms,
• Solid Python and PyTorch/HuggingFace, and comfortable with segmentation and detection architectures,
• Strong interest in computer vision and women’s health. A first experience with medical images is a plus,
• You speak English and ideally French.
