Ours already runs two orders of magnitude faster than hardware (tens of thousands of episodes in half an hour instead of 200+ hours), while correlating with on-hardware rollouts at 89%. The north star: physical AI that improves at the speed of compute.

The role

Simulation is still a hard sell in robotics. Outside a few success stories, like reinforcement learning for locomotion, most teams skip it, and friction is a big part of why: painful to use, painful to debug. We live that pain ourselves: debugging a failing experiment during policy evaluation takes 30 minutes, and there is no way to automatically generate a standalone reproduction script. That blocks adoption, even internally.

Your job is to kill that friction. You build the software engineering backbone of Genesis-World: everything that makes a large, fast-moving simulation codebase reliable, maintainable, frictionless. And it all ships in the open. Every hour of pain you remove, you remove for every roboticist who comes after you.

You join as core maintainer of Genesis-World, with shared stewardship of the whole platform from day one. Our physics team develops the algorithms, but just as importantly, you work to make everything around them excellent: infrastructure, tooling, APIs, architecture.

The problems waiting for you

- Make testing of a JIT-compiled engine scalable. Running our full suite is already taking hours because the ratio between compile time and runtime can be as bad as x10. Getting rid of this bottleneck is a serious challenge that will require a joint effort from the Genesis-World and the compiler teams.

- Make any bug reproducible. Dump and reload simulations bit-exactly, across machines, across backends, even when a single timestep of a batched simulation can already max out VRAM. Turn any failing run into a standalone reproduction script, automatically.

- Make autodiff first-class. Genesis-World is differentiable today, but partially: memory-hungry, slower than it could be, and hard to maintain due to manual operation recording. The project spans the engine and the compiler: you drive the requirements on Quadrants and iterate in a tight loop with the compiler team until the integration is solid.

- Edit scenes at frozen time. See the scene, move entities and robots around, iterate on layout, all without building the scene or compiling the engine. Authoring today means a full build cycle. Make it instant.

- Make the simulator extensible. First-class plugins for physics solvers and interactive viewer backends, including Nyx. Sensors already work this way. Generalize it, and Genesis-World becomes a platform others build on.

- Give robots real actuation. Motors and MIMO transmissions, cleanly abstracted at the interface between users and the physics engine.

- Make time a local variable. Today the clock and the timestep are global to the engine, which forbids whole classes of speedups: environments cannot step independently, the timestep cannot adapt to the state, and individual solvers cannot advance at their own rate. Free the clock down to the sub-scene level and let the simulation fly.

- Make scenes come alive. Events triggered by physics: press the button and the microwave door pops open, squeeze the trigger and the drill spins.

- Keep the core sharp. Refactoring legacy subsystems, stronger typing, consistent coding style, less Python overhead on hot paths, full scene serialization, telemetry and replay.

Beyond the code: you review issues and pull requests with the core team, answer questions from users and contributors, and can join the push on adoption.

Who you are

You care about the engineer using what you build as much as the thing itself. A slow test, a cryptic error, a manual step: you see it, you go after the root cause, and you remove it for everyone. You have opinions about API design.

You are comfortable with physics and robotics: the right design choices take a working picture of what a simulator like Genesis-World does, how it works, and how it is used, a picture you can partly build on the job.

- Strong Python engineering on large codebases: architecture, refactoring, typing, packaging, performance profiling (py-spy, Nsight, Xcode Instruments, RenderDoc).

- Developer tooling, test infrastructure, or CI at scale.

- Enough fluency with JIT compilation, code generation, or GPU computing stacks to reason about compilation caching, kernel dispatch, and startup cost. You will work closely with Quadrants.

- At ease debugging across the full platform matrix: Windows, Linux, and macOS, on x86 and arm64, over CUDA, AMD, and Apple Metal (and possibly Intel XPU via Vulkan soon)

- Open-source reflexes: triaging issues, reviewing external pull requests, communicating with a community.

Bonus points: experience with other robotics simulators (Drake, MuJoCo, Newton, Isaac, RaiSim, Jiminy, Brax). PyTorch, our user-facing interface. Other JIT compilers such as Triton, JAX, or Numba. 3D tooling and interactive editors (Maya, Blender, Houdini). Serialization formats (USD, glTF, MJCF/URDF). C++, CUDA, or Metal. Developer relations or community work.

description:

About your role 

As the Director, Engineering you will lead the vision and execution for the foundational systems that power our entire engineering organization. Your mandate spans four critical pillars: architecting the modularization of our core Python/FastAPI monolith, accelerating our transition to an AI-native engineering culture, empowering product teams with tools to build AI-enabled features, and establishing a robust Application Security (AppSec) posture.

Lead Application Security (AppSec): Champion a "shift-left" security culture. Embed secure coding practices, automated vulnerability scanning, and threat modeling directly into developer workflows, ensuring our core platform is resilient against modern threats.

- 
Oversee Core Shared Services: Drive the scale, security, and reliability of enterprise-critical systems, including Identity (AuthN/AuthZ, OAuth2, RBAC), Audit Logs, and high-throughput API & MCP Gateways.

- 
Navigate Org-Wide Boundaries: Negotiate complex refactoring timelines with Product leaders and collaborate seamlessly with other Engineering teams and DevOps to align our platform capabilities with infrastructure.

Build a World-Class Organization: Recruit, mentor, and grow a high-performing organization of engineering managers and staff/principal engineers, fostering a culture of architectural pragmatism and deep developer empathy.

title: Technical Product Manager
description:
About Kernel

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent Kernel ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. We have strong product-market fit: Ops, data, and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva, and Checkout already use Kernel across their enterprise systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators, and we are growing 12x YoY .

The role 

You will own one of Kernel’s product areas end-to-end, working directly with the founders and the engineering team

- Own all stages from discovery to implementation for our core product areas and bets

What we’re looking for

We are looking for a full-stack product thinker who can own and lead product work from discovery to implementation.

- Evals: Comfortable with evals for agents and driving quality improvements via evals and recursive self-improvement

- Prefer long cycles and big “reveals.”

title: Neuroscientist
description:

The Role 

Netholabs is building AI grounded in biological intelligence. We record petascale, high-resolution neurobehavioural data from living systems and use it to train neural foundation models — a new substrate for the next generation of AI, robotics, and personalised intelligence. We aim to greatly reduce the burden of animals used in basic scientific research and pharmacological work, with eventual removal and replacement by in silico models.

We're looking for a Neuroscientist to join our Brighton research team as an independent contributor driving experiments from design through analysis. You'll design and run in vivo electrophysiology and behavioural experiments, work with large-scale neural and behavioural datasets, and partner closely with our ML team to translate what we learn about real brains and bodies into better foundation models. This is a role for someone who wants their science to feed directly into what gets built next.

Responsibilities 

In Vivo Electrophysiology & Neural Recording 

- Design and run in vivo electrophysiology experiments in animal models

- Develop and refine neural recording protocols and rigs alongside the hardware team

- Ensure recordings meet the quality and fidelity standards our models are trained on

Behavioural Neuroscience & Experimental Design 

- Design behavioural paradigms that generate rich, well-controlled datasets

- Plan and oversee data collection sessions, in collaboration with technicians

- Iterate on experimental design based on data quality and downstream modelling needs

Data Analysis & Computational Modelling 

- Analyse large-scale neural and behavioural datasets

- Build and apply computational models to characterise neural and behavioural dynamics

Neuroscience → AI Translation

- Help define what neurobehavioural data and features are most valuable to capture

Requirements

- Strong data analysis skills, including experience with Python or a similar language

- Excellent communication; comfortable working cross-functionally with engineering and ML teams

Valued (or willing to learn) 

- Experience with large-scale or multi-modal neurobehavioural datasets

- Familiarity with machine learning fundamentals or foundation model training

- Experience with computational modelling of neural or behavioural data

- Prior work bridging neuroscience and AI/robotics research

We are revolutionizing the space industry with ground-breaking innovations that allow us to offer the best performance to cost propulsion systems.

Our goal is to be the propulsion provider for the next generation of spacecraft, which is essential to meet demands and compete in the booming space market of the next decade. We are a passionate, multicultural, and multidisciplinary team pushing the boundaries of what is possible in space propulsion technology. We have already made history by successfully testing the world's first 3D-printed Methalox Aerospike engine, marking a significant milestone for the space industry. We are looking for talented professionals to join our international teams in Barcelona and Toulouse.

We want to be a key player in improving diversity in the Aerospace sector as, in Pangea, we believe that diversity (gender, age, race, sexual orientation, beliefs, disability, culture, etc.) is a key to success. Within Pangea, everyone can grow with the same opportunities. We encourage you to apply. Individually we are different, but together we are an amazing team!

We are looking for a CFD Workflow Automation Intern for a 6-month internship in Toulouse.

About the role: 

We are seeking a highly skilled intern with a strong programming background and an interest in engineering simulation to help automate repetitive CFD activities across the Turbomachinery Fluidic Design Team and the Fluidic Analysis Team.

The role will focus on developing robust, reusable workflows for meshing, simulation setup and launching, data extraction, post-processing, and standardized reporting, with particular emphasis on Cadence and Ansys Fluent environments. The internship is intended to reduce manual effort, improve repeatability, and shorten analysis turnaround time across the Fluidics Department.

The intern will work with engineers from both teams to identify high-value automation opportunities, translate existing engineering practices into scripts and workflows, and validate the resulting tools on representative analysis cases. Prior expertise in Cadence or Ansys Fluent is not required; strong programming ability and a willingness to learn the relevant engineering applications are more important.

Key Responsibilities: 

• Develop scripts and utilities to automate CFD meshing, simulation setup, job launching, monitoring, and post-processing activities.

• Automate recurring workflows in Cadence and Ansys Fluent, using the scripting and interface capabilities available within those environments.

• Create reusable tools for data extraction, visualization, comparison, and standardized reporting of CFD results. • Work with the Turbomachinery Fluidic Design Team to streamline the design-analysis iteration loop, including comparison of CFD results with design intent.

• Work with the Fluidic Analysis Team to identify repetitive analysis tasks and convert them into reliable, maintainable automated processes.

• Define input requirements, verification checks, error handling, and user documentation so that the developed tools can be adopted by different engineers.

• Validate automated workflows against existing manual processes and document accuracy, repeatability, limitations, and expected time savings.

• Present progress and results to the participating teams and incorporate user feedback into successive tool improvements.

What you need to be successful: 

• Final-year student or recent graduate in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field.

• Strong programming skills, preferably in Python; experience with additional scripting languages is an advantage.

• Understanding of software development fundamentals, including modular code, version control, testing, debugging, and documentation.

• Ability to analyse an existing manual workflow, identify repetitive steps, and translate the process into a structured automation solution.

• Interest in CFD, numerical simulation, engineering data processing, or scientific computing. Previous application-specific experience is not mandatory.

• Fluency in written and spoken English.

Soft Skills: 

• Analytical and methodical approach to problem solving.

• Proactive mindset and willingness to take ownership of a defined work package.

• Clear communication and ability to gather requirements from engineers in different teams.

• Attention to detail, with a focus on reliability, traceability, and usability.

• Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively in a multicultural, multidisciplinary environment.

Other useful skills: 

• Experience with engineering or scientific Python and Matlab libraries for data processing and visualization.

• Familiarity with Linux, command-line tools, batch processing, high-performance computing, or job schedulers.

• Exposure to APIs, graphical user interfaces, dashboards, or automated report generation.

• Familiarity with Git or another version-control system.

• Previous exposure to Cadence, Ansys Fluent, CFD meshing, or simulation postprocessing is beneficial but not required.

• Basic knowledge of fluid dynamics or numerical methods is an advantage.

Supervision and collaboration: 

The intern will be supervised by a designated engineer and will collaborate with representatives of both the Turbomachinery Fluidic Design Team and the Fluidic Analysis Team. The assignment will be managed as a shared departmental initiative, with priorities defined according to the automation needs and potential impact identified by the participating teams.

We are seeking a motivated System Performance Intern to join our System Performance team in Toulouse. During this six-month internship, you will support system-level design, modelling and performance analysis activities for Kronos full-flow staged-combustion rocket engines.

You will work closely with System Performance engineers and specialists in combustion, fluidics, turbomachinery and other disciplines to connect engine requirements and design choices with cycle modelling, subsystem characteristics and overall engine performance. You will be involved in the development and execution of engine models, investigating nominal, throttled and off-nominal operating conditions, and assessing how evolving subsystem designs influence the complete propulsion system. The work will include sensitivity studies, design trade-offs and support to the definition of operating and control strategies.

This internship requires strong fundamentals in thermodynamics and fluid mechanics, an understanding of liquid rocket-engine cycles, and the ability to interpret numerical results critically rather than treating simulation tools as black boxes. You will contribute to transient analyses covering start-up, throttling and shutdown, and consolidate results into engineering conclusions, performance maps, operating envelopes, subsystem requirements and technical documentation for design reviews.

· Analyse nominal operating points and engine operational envelopes, including throttled and off-nominal conditions.

· Support engine-cycle optimisation and system-level design trade-offs.

· Perform sensitivity studies on key design and operational parameters.

· Translate simulation results into engineering conclusions, performance maps, operating envelopes and subsystem requirements.

· Support preparation and maintenance of System Performance documentation for project design reviews.

· Work with combustion, fluidics, turbomachinery and other disciplines to integrate evolving subsystem designs into the system model.

What you need to be successful: 

· MSc in Aerospace Engineering or equivalent, preferably with a background in propulsion, fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, energy systems or numerical modelling.

· Experience with numerical modelling and engineering analysis through academic or professional projects.

· Strong fundamentals in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics and heat transfer.

· Understanding of liquid rocket propulsion and the fundamental operation of rocket-engine cycles.

· Ability to analyse coupled engineering systems and critically interpret simulation results.

· Basic programming or engineering scripting capability, preferably Python and/or MATLAB.

Soft Skills: 

· Strong analytical problem-solving skills.

· Ability to communicate technical results clearly in English through documentation and presentations.

· You are expected to work in a structured and analytical manner, communicate your results clearly, and progressively take ownership of defined modelling and analysis tasks while receiving guidance from experienced engineers.

We are looking for a Rocket Engine Injector Modelling and Design Tool Development intern for a 6-month internship in Toulouse. 

About the role 

We are looking for a motivated engineering intern to join our Combustion Devices team and contribute to the development of engineering tools supporting the design and analysis of liquid rocket engine injectors.

During this internship, you will work on computational tools to automate and accelerate the preliminary design and assessment of injector configurations.

Your work will focus on three main areas:

- Injector layout & manifold modelling: develop tools to automate injector element layouts and associated fuel and oxidiser manifolds, based on geometrical, fluid-dynamic and engineering design rules.
- Injector spray-pattern visualisation: develop a qualitative visualisation of spray/jet directions, cone angles, spatial coverage and interactions between neighbouring injector elements.
- Face-plate thermal assessment: contribute to a physics-based methodology to assess thermal loads based on injector configuration, local mixture ratio, spray angle, injection conditions and combustion behaviour.

The developed tools will support the team in rapidly comparing injector configurations, identifying potential performance and thermal risks, and improving the overall preliminary design process.

Key Responsibilities 

- Review existing injector design methodologies, engineering rules and relevant technical literature.

- Define relevant CFD analysis needs and interpret available CFD and experimental data.
- Validate models and tools against available analytical, numerical, experimental or literature data.
- Document methodologies, assumptions, limitations and recommendations for future development and integration into the Combustion Devices design process.

- Final-year student or recent graduate in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Software Engineering , or a related technical field.
- Strong programming skills, particularly in MATLAB and Python .
- Good understanding of: - Fluid mechanics
- Thermodynamics and heat transfer
- Numerical methods and computational modelling

- Experience with data processing, numerical analysis or scientific computing.
- Ability to translate physical and engineering requirements into computational models and algorithms.
- Ability to analyse numerical results and identify relevant physical trends.
- Critical thinking when assessing modelling assumptions and engineering correlations.
- Interest in rocket propulsion, combustion devices and liquid-propellant injection systems .
- Fluent written and spoken English.

Soft Skills 

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Autonomous, structured and methodical approach.
- Curiosity and willingness to explore unfamiliar technical topics.
- Ability to collaborate within a multicultural and multidisciplinary engineering team.
- Good technical communication and documentation skills.
- Attention to detail and critical thinking.

Nice to have 

Any of the following would be a plus, but is not required :

- Experience with liquid rocket engine injectors, combustion chambers or other combustion systems.
- Knowledge of coaxial, impinging-jet, swirl or pintle injectors.
- Knowledge of multiphase flows, sprays, atomisation or propellant mixing.
- Knowledge of combustion physics, reacting flows or turbulent heat transfer.
- Experience with thermal modelling or heat-transfer correlations.
- Experience with CFD tools, post-processing or interpretation of reacting-flow/heat-transfer simulations.
- Experience analysing parameters such as local mixture ratio, spray angle, wall heat flux or wall temperature.
- Experience developing engineering correlations from numerical or experimental data.
- Experience with geometrical algorithms, optimisation or automated engineering design tools.
- Experience developing graphical interfaces or engineering visualisation tools.
- Familiarity with Git or other version-control tools.

Expected internship outcomes 

By the end of the internship, you will have contributed to:

- A functional MATLAB/Python tool for automated injector layout and manifold definition.
- An injector spray-pattern visualisation tool .
- A preliminary physics-based methodology for assessing injector face-plate thermal loads .
- Validation of the developed methodologies against available literature, CFD, experimental or reference data.
- Technical documentation covering the tools, methodologies, assumptions, limitations and recommendations for future integration.

Supervision and collaboration 

You will be supervised by an engineer from the Combustion Devices team and collaborate closely with the future users of the tools. Technical priorities, verification cases and acceptance criteria will be reviewed regularly to ensure that the tools address practical engineering needs.

title: DevOps, Core Platform

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the role

We are building software infrastructure to power AI development and delivery for operational use cases in defense. Our software needs to run in customers' data centers, on their hardware, often with no internet connection. You will own the continuous deployment of our software in these environments. That covers installations, upgrades with no downtime, and keeping track of dependencies between the services that make up the software.

This role involves hands-on coding. You will join the core platform team, with broad ownership and a direct effect on real defense deployments.

Responsibilities

- Delivery: Take a change from a commit in CI to a running system on a customer site, and keep every step repeatable.

- Safe upgrades: Roll out upgrades step by step with no downtime, watch the system as it changes, and stop and alert the team automatically when something goes wrong.

- Disconnected sites: Make installs and upgrades work with no internet, using signed, self-contained packages.

- Release checks: Work on the release system that checks that all our services work together, in CI and at release time.

- Collaboration: Work with platform architects and developers so every new service is easy to package, deploy and upgrade. Work with our forward deployed engineers, who install and run the software at customer sites, so the same tools run in development and at the customer.

- Documentation: Write the procedures that a person at a customer site can follow without our help.

- Growth: Make it easier and faster for our engineers to ship changes to customer sites.

Candidate requirements

- Experience: Several years of backend or infrastructure engineering, ideally on a product with many services and many deployments.

- Coding: Strong skills in at least one language (Rust, Go, Python, Java).

- Kubernetes and delivery: Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and containers, and with Helm, GitOps (Argo CD or Flux) and CI systems.

- Builder: You have built, not just used, tools that deploy or run software.

- Production: You have run or debugged upgrades or deployments in production, and you know the basics of metrics, health checks and logs.

- Educational background: Degree in computer science, software engineering or a similar field. Equivalent professional experience is equally valued.

- Language: Clear written and spoken English.

Nice to have

- Writing Kubernetes operators or controllers.

- Signing and supply-chain tools, such as Sigstore/cosign and SBOMs.

- Packaging software for air-gapped sites, for example with Zarf and registry mirrors such as Harbor.

- Bare-metal Kubernetes (OpenShift, RKE2 or Talos) with Ceph or MinIO.

Mindset

- Pragmatic engineering: You choose simple solutions and proven tools first.

- Attention to detail: You obsess over edge cases and robustness before you ship a change.

- User-oriented: You treat other engineers as your users. You take care designing APIs and tools that are simple and pleasant to use.

- Ownership: You take responsibility for ensuring the project works regardless of your job description.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

title: Deployment Strategist
description:

About the Team 

The FDE (Forward Deployed Engineering) team is a new, strategic initiative sponsored from the CEO and Founders down. Our mission is to win C-suite-sponsored, high-value AI opportunities by selling and delivering outcomes , not just a platform.

You will be part of the founding team, embedded with our most strategic customers from the very first sales call, all the way through to a production-ready solution. You will be the "product manager" for the customer's problem, responsible for the "why" and "what," while our FDEs (Engineers) will be your partners responsible for the "how."

Role Description 

As a Deployment Strategist (DS), you are the critical bridge between a customer's multi-million-dollar business problem and Databricks' technical solution. You are a product manager for the field, owning the technical and product direction of the engagement from initial discovery through production launch and adoption.

You will build C-suite trust, perform deep discovery to map the customer's political and technical landscape, and scope the value. You will define the Minimum Viable Product for a pilot, write the PRD that guides the engineering team, and manage the project to a successful landing. You will also lead technical discovery, shape solution architecture with FDEs, and ensure that each proposed solution can move from prototype to production.

This role requires a rare combination of executive presence, deep product thinking, technical depth, and a hands-on delivery mindset.

The impact you will have 

- C-Suite Scoping & Value Definition: Partner with Sales to perform deep discovery, map the customer's organization, quantify the business value of $10M+ problems, and define the pilot, including its MVP, success criteria, and timeline.

- End-to-End Product Ownership: Author the PRD, prioritize the engineering backlog, manage scope, and act as the primary hands-on QA tester. Translate business requirements into clear data, integration, security, and operational requirements that engineers can build against.

- Technical Solution Leadership & Delivery: Drive the FDE build team through an agile delivery process, manage stakeholders from the C-suite to individual engineers, and unblock technical or organizational issues. Lead technical discovery and design reviews. Understand the customer's data flows, integrations, platform constraints, and operational environment; pressure-test architecture choices; and identify technical risks early.

- Solution Launch & Landing: Own the "Day 0" launch, manage the war room, and drive the solution from launch to full adoption by capturing user feedback, iterating, and proving the defined business value. Own production readiness across data quality, testing, security, performance, and operations. Work with the team to diagnose issues and drive them to resolution.

- Strategic Handoff & Growth: Scope the ongoing maintenance plan, create customer documentation/training, and leverage your trusted advisor status to identify the next high-value FDE engagement. Codify reusable solution patterns and bring field insights back to Product and Engineering.

What we look for 

- Executive Presence & Communication: You are a trusted advisor with strong executive presence and excellent communication skills. You are confident and humble, can build rapport quickly, and can help senior stakeholders make difficult decisions.

- Product Judgment & Delivery: You can define what to build and why, write strong product requirements, prioritize engineering work, manage scope, and lead complex agile software projects from an ambiguous problem to a measurable outcome.

- Technical Fluency & Architecture Judgment: You understand modern data and AI architectures, including cloud platforms, data pipelines, data models, distributed systems, APIs, security and governance, machine learning, and generative AI application patterns. You can lead architecture discussions, evaluate trade-offs, and pressure-test technical decisions.

- Relevant Experience: Typically 7+ years of experience delivering complex, customer-facing data, analytics, AI, or software engagements, or equivalent experience as a founder or technical builder. You have helped deliver data, machine learning, or generative AI systems into production and understand the integration, operational, and adoption challenges that appear in real environments. Experience in a high-growth technology company, forward-deployed organization, or leading consultancy is valuable. title: Staff Software Engineer - Alwin
description:
We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer in our Amsterdam office to build Alwin , our Agentic Automation Platform for audit and finance, and the systems around it. Alwin agents run multi-step audit procedures over client evidence and return finished workpapers with every number traced back to source. Humans plan, review and sign off.

This is a hands-on role: most of your time will be spent writing code, building the hardest parts of the runtime, prototyping new capabilities and getting them into production. You lead by example: engineers follow your direction because they see it work in your code. Your impact will also come through the engineers and teams you work with.

Your mission is to build the best agentic runtime for audit: one that completes audit tasks faster, more accurately, more reliably and at lower cost, while scaling to meet the needs of our largest customers.

You will identify the problems that most constrain that mission, align teams around a technical direction and drive solutions through to measurable results, while building the foundations other engineers use and raising the quality of Alwin’s agents in production.

Why DataSnipper? 

The hardest AI problems aren't about getting an answer fast. They're about getting one people can trust. 

We believe trust is essential to how society works. Every day, we rely on information that's been independently verified, from financial statements to the products we buy, to the sustainability claims companies make. Behind that trust are audit and finance professionals who examine evidence, verify information and hold organizations accountable.

At DataSnipper, we build AI solutions that empower those professionals. By making evidence easier to trace and verify, we help them focus on the judgment and expertise that make their work so important.

For our product and engineering team, this is where things get exciting. In audit, a plausible answer isn't good enough. Every output has to be explainable and traceable back to its source. We've just launched a brand new agentic platform, Alwin by DataSnipper. AI agents running in the cloud across hundreds of documents at once, reasoning across PDF, Word and Excel, with a full audit trail behind every step. There are lots of greenfield problems ahead, and real room to shape what we build and how we build it.

And we build at scale. More than 600,000 professionals across 3,000+ organizations in 175 countries rely on DataSnipper, including Fortune 500 companies, government agencies and all Big Four audit firms. In 2025 alone, the DataSnipper platform delivered more than $1.4 billion in productivity savings to is customers . Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, and as proud members of 1% for the Planet, we care about how we grow, not just how fast.

If you want to build AI that professionals trust with work that really matters, this is your chance to help shape the future of audit and finance and do the best work of your career along the way. 

What You Will Do: 

Results You Will Drive 

- Better audit outcomes: improve how accurately and reliably agents complete real audit tasks, with traceable results and human oversight.

- A faster, more efficient runtime: reduce execution time and cost while scaling to more complex workloads and larger customers.

- More capable teams: build foundations and feedback loops that multiple teams use to ship and improve agents faster.

Build & Ship

- Champion experimentation and R&D : try emerging models and techniques, solve hard problems creatively, and turn promising ideas into reliable features

- Build shared capabilities that multiple teams adopt , and remain accountable for whether they make those teams faster and their products more reliable

Agents in Production

Lead by Example

What You Bring:

Nice-to-Have

title: Internship - Programming & Automation
description:
WE CANNOT PROVIDE VISA SPONSORSHIP 

Details

Preferred starting date: ASAP

Weekly availability: Full-time (5 days/week)

Period: 6 months

Location: Aerospace Innovation Hub, Delft, the Netherlands

About the company

Fiducial is a young but fast-growing deep-tech start-up with big ambitions at the frontier of autonomy, perception, and defence. Currently, we are developing software for advanced onboard UAV situational awareness in military applications. Using low-cost and widely available sensors and compute, our solutions are built for scalability. From there, we plan to develop a line-up of interconnected solutions to safeguard European safety.

Our team consists of engineers who are passionate about the technology and solutions they develop. The only time most of us are not thinking about the technology is when we are asleep, and sometimes even then. Our team members come from different backgrounds such as Aerospace Engineering, Computational Science and Engineering, Robotics, and Computer Graphics. Our office is located in the Aerospace Innovation Hub, a start-up hub on the TU Delft campus in the Faculty of Aerospace Engineering.

We work closely with top-tier partners, ranging from government agencies and prime contractors to academic research institutes and other start-ups. Our projects span from large tender orders in collaboration with partners to low-TRL research with government agencies. Whether through formal R&D programs or rapid prototyping tracks, we operate at the intersection of innovation and deployment.

The project 

Sensor calibration is a manual job today, and it does not scale to the number of sensor units we intend to ship. We are building automated test and calibration infrastructure to fix that, starting with a cell built around a UFactory UF850 robotic arm on a linear rail.

We already have the arm and the calibration software. What we do not have is the physical cell around it, or the software that drives it. This first project is split into two internships that run side by side:

• Robot programming and automation — this position

• Mechanical design and integration — separate posting

The two interns will work closely together. Neither half of this project is any good on its own. This calibration cell is the first thing we are building on this front, not the last, so there is a good chance the right person carries on to other robotics and automation projects once it is running.

Your role 

If you are the kind of person who is not satisfied until an automated system actually works reliably, not just once, this internship is designed for you.

We are looking for a Robot Programming & Automation Intern to help build the software behind our robotic test and automation infrastructure. Your first project is turning a robotic arm on a linear rail into a system that reliably captures good calibration data — but the skills involved are the same ones we’ll lean on for whatever we automate next: getting a robot to move well, knowing whether the data it’s collecting is any good, and building something solid enough to run unattended.

Getting that right is the substance of this internship, on this project and on whatever comes after it.

What you’ll do 

• Build the robot control layer: drive the arm through its SDK, coordinate the linear rail, and plan safe motion inside a cell that also has a target, cables, and an operator in it.

• Design pose generation that’s actually informed by the calibration problem, including getting proper coverage across a multi-camera rig rather than just one lens at a time.

• Get the timing and synchronisation right between the robot, the cameras, and the captured data — this is where automated rigs usually go wrong.

• Gate data quality at capture time, and retry within the run rather than finding out later that a dataset is unusable.

• Close the loop with our existing calibration pipeline: feed it data, read back its results, and use that to decide what to capture next and when a run is done.

• Package captures with the metadata needed to make a calibration reproducible, and make the whole thing robust to failures mid-run.

• Build a simple operator-facing workflow: mount the rig, pick a profile, press go.

• Work closely with the mechanical intern — your requirements shape their fixture design, and their measurements shape your motion limits.

Who you are 

• You are enrolled in a relevant study program (Robotics, Computer Science, Computational Science and Engineering, Mechatronics, Aerospace, Electrical Engineering, or similar).

• You are strong in Python. C++ is a plus.

• You are comfortable with 3D geometry: rigid transforms, rotation representations, coordinate frames, and keeping your conventions straight when it is 6pm and nothing lines up.

• You are interested in robot programming specifically — motion, reachability, collisions, repeatability — and not only in the vision maths around it.

• You understand enough about how camera calibration works to reason about what makes a dataset good or useless. You do not need to be able to write the solver.

• You have worked with real sensors and real robots, and you have learned that they lie about timing.

• You care about reliability. An automated process that works four times out of five is not automated.

• You write code that another engineer can pick up and extend.

• You are comfortable taking responsibility for software that moves physical hardware.

• You are independent, curious, organized, and resourceful.

• Linux does not scare you, and neither does a robot that moves the moment your code says move.

We care much more about what you have built and made work than about grades.

Nice to have 

These are strong pluses, but not strict requirements:

• ROS 2, MoveIt 2, tf2, and motion planning in practice

• Experience with industrial or collaborative arm SDKs (UFactory / xArm, UR, Franka), or motion control more generally

• Hands-on camera calibration experience: OpenCV, Kalibr, ChArUco or AprilTag targets, hand-eye calibration

• Multi-camera rigs, and the specific pain of calibrating cameras with little or no overlapping field of view

• Machine vision cameras: triggering and synchronisation, GenICam, exposure control, rolling versus global shutter

• Coverage or observability reasoning: understanding why some poses inform a parameter and others do not

• Simulation environments (Gazebo, Isaac Sim, MuJoCo)

• Docker, CI, and the habit of writing tests before you need them

• Experience turning a research script into something an operator can actually use

Please include 

When applying, please include links, repositories, or writeups that show us you build things that work. For example:

• GitHub repositories, with a note on which parts you actually wrote

• robot arm or robot motion projects

• camera calibration, multi-view geometry, SLAM, or structure-from-motion work

• data capture pipelines, test automation, or anything that had to run unattended

• computer vision projects

• simulation work

• a short writeup of something that broke and how you found the cause

• anything that demonstrates hands-on technical ownership

If you have ever chased a calibration error you couldn’t explain, eventually traced it to a timestamp, and fixed it properly, you’ll probably fit right in.

Requirements 

• Enrolled in a relevant study program (Robotics, Computer Science, CSE, Mechatronics, Aerospace, Electrical Engineering, or similar)

• Strong programming skills, Python at minimum

• Comfortable working in Linux

• Strong interest in robotics, automation, computer vision, or perception

• English proficiency

• Organized and proactive working style

What we offer 

• 1000 euro monthly compensation

• 10 vacation days during the internship period

• Flexible working hours and the option to work from home 2 days per week where practical

• A direct and significant influence on highly innovative products

• The opportunity to work close to the hardware and the product, with fast iteration and tight feedback loops

• Full ownership of a self-contained system that the rest of the company will depend on

• A team environment where practical experimentation, learning, and ownership are expected

The application procedure 

• If after reading the above you are convinced you are the right person for the job, send us some information about yourself. This can be a resume, website, portfolio, or any other source that gives us a clear impression of your background, technical skills, and hands-on experience.

• We will get back to you ASAP. If we think you could be a fit for the position, we will invite you for an informal introduction so we can get to know you, and equally important, you can get to know us. After this, a more technically focused interview may follow.

• If at that point we believe you are the person we are looking for, we will discuss the specifics such as starting date and internship period.

Welcome to the team!

title: Senior Full-Stack Growth Engineer - Marketing & Analytics
description:
About Truelogic 

At Truelogic we are a leading provider of nearshore staff augmentation services headquartered in New York. For over two decades, we’ve been delivering top-tier technology solutions to companies of all sizes, from innovative startups to industry leaders, helping them achieve their digital transformation goals.

Our team of 600+ highly skilled tech professionals, based in Latin America, drives digital disruption by partnering with U.S. companies on their most impactful projects. Whether collaborating with Fortune 500 giants or scaling startups, we deliver results that make a difference.

By applying for this position, you’re taking the first step in joining a dynamic team that values your expertise and aspirations. We aim to align your skills with opportunities that foster exceptional career growth and success while contributing to transformative projects that shape the future.

Our Client 

A premier digital product and technology consulting firm specializing in modern software engineering, cloud-native architecture, and strategic digital transformation across high-impact sectors including healthcare, financial services, and education.

Job Summary 

The Senior Full-Stack Growth Engineer plays a pivotal role in designing, building, and evolving the technical infrastructure that powers customer acquisition, experimentation, and marketing performance. This unique position bridges end-to-end full-stack software development with rigorous quantitative analysis to drive measurable business impact. The ideal candidate will architect production features and internal tools, build resilient API and CRM integrations, instrument deep product analytics, and design statistically sound experiments across the entire user lifecycle. Collaborating closely with cross-functional product, design, and growth teams, this role turns critical business hypotheses into high-impact, shippable solutions supported by clean data and causal measurement.

Responsibilities 

- 
Architect, build, and maintain production-ready full-stack features, backend services, web applications, and internal growth tools.

- 
Design, deploy, and evaluate experiments across customer acquisition, onboarding flows, conversion funnels, and retention loops.

- 
Apply statistical inference and causal reasoning to evaluate A/B test results, identify confounding factors, and communicate uncertainty clearly to stakeholders.

- 
Implement robust event tracking, instrumentation, and product analytics using modern platforms (e.g., PostHog).

- 
Integrate advertising platforms, CRMs, databases, and third-party tools via REST/GraphQL APIs, webhooks, and event-driven data pipelines.

- 
Evolve database schemas and analytical data models to support new product workflows, attribution, and reliable measurement.

- 
Connect acquisition, product usage, CRM, and revenue data streams to analyze full-funnel customer journeys and business outcomes.

- 
Maintain high standards for data quality, automated testing, observability, user privacy, and data security across all integrations.

- 
Collaborate with marketing, product, and design partners to translate strategic growth objectives into testable engineering roadmaps.

- 
Leverage modern AI-assisted engineering and analytical workflows responsibly, ensuring rigorous validation and data governance.

Qualifications and Job Requirements 

- 
Proven track record as a Full-Stack Software Engineer building modern web applications, scalable backend APIs, and working with relational databases.

- 
Advanced SQL proficiency alongside hands-on scripting/analytical experience in Python, R, or equivalent modern data tools.

- 
Practical foundation in experimental design, A/B testing methodologies, statistical inference, and causal reasoning.

- 
Hands-on experience implementing product analytics instrumentation, event pipelines, and auditing data quality.

- 
Solid experience architecting third-party integrations using webhooks, APIs, and event-driven patterns.

- 
Strong ability to translate complex data findings and technical tradeoffs into actionable business and product insights.

- 
Practical experience with AI-assisted software development and analytical tooling, backed by sound engineering judgment regarding validation and security.

Preferred / Nice to Have: 

- 
Familiarity with PostHog, CRM platforms, marketing automation engines, Conversion APIs (CAPI), or server-side tracking.

- 
Familiarity with growth metrics such as CAC, LTV, churn/retention curves, and ROAS.

- 
Understanding of incrementality testing, conversion lift studies, and attribution model nuances.

- 
Background in consulting, client-facing delivery, or building software in regulated environments (e.g., healthcare, fintech).

What We Offer 

- 
100% Remote Work: Enjoy the freedom to work from the location that helps you thrive. All it takes is a laptop and a reliable internet connection.

- 
Highly Competitive USD Pay: Earn an excellent, market-leading compensation in USD, that goes beyond typical market offerings.

- 
Paid Time Off: We value your well-being. Our paid time off policies ensure you have the chance to unwind and recharge when needed.

- 
Work with Autonomy: Enjoy the freedom to manage your time as long as the work gets done. Focus on results, not the clock.

- 
Work with Top American Companies: Grow your expertise working on innovative, high-impact projects with Industry-Leading U.S. Companies.

Why You’ll Like Working Here 

- 
A Culture That Values You: We prioritize well-being and work-life balance, offering engagement activities and fostering dynamic teams to ensure you thrive both personally and professionally.

- 
Diverse, Global Network: Connect with over 600 professionals in 25+ countries, expand your network, and collaborate with a multicultural team from Latin America.

- 
Team Up with Skilled Professionals: Join forces with senior talent. All of our team members are seasoned experts, ensuring you're working with the best in your field.

Apply now!

title: Agentic AI Senior Consultant
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Agentic AI Senior Consultant based in Switzerland. 

In this role, you will act as a trusted technical advisor and hands-on engineering expert, helping enterprise customers design, implement, and scale advanced agentic AI solutions. You will lead the entire customer delivery lifecycle, from identifying high-value business opportunities and designing multi-agent architectures to deploying production-ready systems. Combining strong software engineering expertise, applied AI knowledge, and event-driven architecture experience, you will transform AI concepts into secure, scalable, and reliable enterprise applications. You will work closely with customer engineering teams, business stakeholders, and internal product specialists to accelerate the adoption of intelligent automation. Your responsibilities will also include establishing best practices for agent development, evaluation, monitoring, and governance while mentoring other technical professionals. This is an opportunity to work at the forefront of enterprise AI innovation within an international, customer-focused, and technically ambitious environment.

Accountabilities: 

- Own the technical success of enterprise customers' agentic AI initiatives, managing the complete delivery lifecycle from initial discovery and solution design through development, production deployment, ongoing operations, and advisory services.

- Lead customer workshops to identify, assess, and prioritize high-value agentic AI use cases, translating business objectives into measurable and technically achievable workflows.

- Design and implement sophisticated multi-agent architectures, including agent decomposition, orchestration, task delegation, tool integration, memory management, state handling, and human-in-the-loop controls.

- Develop, review, and troubleshoot production-quality software using Go or Python, building agents, plugins, tools, and integrations that meet enterprise requirements.

- Deploy and operate agentic AI applications using Docker, Kubernetes, and major cloud platforms, ensuring scalability, reliability, and maintainability.

- Integrate AI agents with enterprise applications, data sources, and legacy systems through MCP servers, A2A protocols, REST APIs, and event-driven messaging architectures.

- Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), vector databases, knowledge bases, embeddings, and real-time event context strategies to improve agent accuracy and access to relevant information.

- Apply the Agent Development Lifecycle (ADLC) throughout solution delivery, covering requirements gathering, architecture design, evaluation pipelines, testing, version control, release management, monitoring, and operational documentation.

- Establish robust observability, security controls, governance frameworks, and responsible AI practices for agentic systems, including tracing, quality evaluation, cost and latency monitoring, access control, and auditability.

- Advise customers on large language model selection and optimization across providers such as Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, AWS Bedrock, and Azure AI Foundry, considering prompt engineering, token consumption, costs, and model performance trade-offs.

- Act as a long-term technical advisor, identifying opportunities for further AI adoption and helping customers progress from isolated pilots to enterprise-wide, event-driven AI implementations.

- Conduct recurring technical reviews, solution health checks, and roadmap discussions aligned with customer priorities and annual planning cycles.

- Enable customer engineering teams to independently operate, maintain, and extend implemented solutions through technical workshops, collaborative development sessions, and comprehensive documentation.

- Develop reusable technical assets, including reference architectures, implementation patterns, accelerators, and best practices, to improve delivery efficiency and consistency across future engagements.

- Represent customer needs and technical feedback to internal Product and Engineering teams, contributing insights that influence product development and roadmap priorities.

- Collaborate closely with agentic AI platform engineering teams to resolve complex customer challenges, validate new capabilities, and contribute reusable agents, plugins, and accelerators.

- Provide technical leadership and mentorship to other professionals, helping strengthen agentic AI expertise and delivery capabilities across the Professional Services organization.

- Communicate complex technical concepts, AI-related risks, and architectural trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Travel when required to support customer engagements, including occasional international travel.

- Strong understanding of software development lifecycle (SDLC) practices, including version control, automated testing, CI/CD, and release management, with practical experience applying a structured Agent Development Lifecycle (ADLC).

- Strong programming proficiency in Go or Python, with Go considered a significant advantage.

- Practical experience designing and implementing multi-agent systems, including task delegation, orchestration, coordination, and autonomous decision-making.

- Familiarity with agent development frameworks such as Google ADK, LangGraph, LangChain, CrewAI, or comparable technologies.

- Solid understanding of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), embeddings, vector databases, prompt engineering, and context management techniques.

- Experience implementing evaluation frameworks, observability solutions, and security guardrails for enterprise LLM applications.

- Strong knowledge of event-driven architectures, asynchronous messaging, distributed systems, and enterprise integration patterns.

- Hands-on experience deploying distributed applications on cloud platforms such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform, using Docker and Kubernetes.

- Understanding of enterprise security and identity management practices relevant to AI systems, including OAuth 2.0, role-based access control (RBAC), secrets management, and data privacy.

- Ability to independently lead customer engagements, make sound technical decisions, and manage complex projects with minimal supervision.

title: Software Development Engineer II (Remote @ Colombia)
description:
Headquarters: Remote @ Colombia

About the role: 

The OfferUp Connect team builds the moments that turn a listing into a sale. Every chat between buyers and sellers, every offer notification, and every saved-search alert runs through services we own, from messaging and notifications to location, meetups, and the subscriptions sellers pay for. We run high-volume Java microservices and streaming pipelines, integrate with partners like Braze, Amazon Pinpoint, Apple, and Google, and use experimentation to decide what ships.

We also take on high-visibility work beyond our domain. Connect built OfferUp's video infrastructure for listing videos and LLM-powered catalog enrichment on Amazon Bedrock, both company priorities that changed what buyers see every day. The roadmap is wide open for someone who wants to help shape it.

As a Software Development Engineer II, you'll own features from concept to rollout: designing and writing well-tested code, launching experiments, and measuring results with Product, Design, and Data partners. You'll raise the quality of the code around you and get the chance to join the next project like video or catalog enrichment.

Here’s more of what you will get to do: 

- Design, build, and deploy backend services and event-driven pipelines for messaging, notifications, location, and subscriptions

- Improve the reliability, latency, and delivery rates of high-volume messaging and notification systems, including retries, rate limiting, and frequency capping

- Integrate with and operate third-party platforms such as Braze, Amazon Pinpoint, Apple and Google push services, and app store billing

- Own features end-to-end: plan, design, develop, deploy, measure, and iterate

- Break down complex engineering problems into achievable tasks and deliver them within committed timeframes

- Work collaboratively with cross-functional teams (Product, Design, Data Science, Marketing, and iOS, Android, and web engineers) to design and implement new features

- Contribute to A/B tests and use experimentation results to decide what ships

- Actively participate in code reviews and enforce good patterns, testing, and edge-case handling

- Coach and mentor junior team members, new hires, and interns

- Create shared components, utilities, and services that improve team velocity across the stack

- Maintain and improve the runbooks, alerting, and monitoring for the features you ship

- Participate in a reasonable on-call rotation with the rest of the team

- Use AI coding tools (Claude Code, Gemini, and similar) to increase your daily development velocity and code quality

- Become a subject matter expert in one or more of the team's sub-domains: messaging, notifications and campaigns, location, or subscriptions and promotions

You’ll thrive in this role if you have: 

- 2+ years of professional software engineering experience

- Demonstrated ability to own the delivery of multiple features end-to-end (plan, design, develop, and deploy) with high efficiency, including breaking down engineering problems into achievable tasks

- Strong coding skills in Java, with a working understanding of microservices and distributed-systems fundamentals

- Good knowledge of data structures and object-oriented design

- Working knowledge of asynchronous, event-driven systems (queues, pub/sub, or streams), including retries and idempotent processing

- Hands-on experience using AI coding tools (Claude Code or similar) in a real engineering workflow, and a point of view on when they help and when they don't

- A habit of following good coding patterns, writing appropriate tests, considering trade-offs, and seeking out edge cases

- Comfortable giving and receiving feedback in code reviews

- A bias toward shipping, learning from production, and iterating quickly

- An insatiable desire and ability to learn

- BS or MS in Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience

Helpful, but not required: 

- Fluency in another modern object-oriented programming language

- Experience with TypeScript and Node.js

- Experience with Agile development

- Experience building and integrating with REST APIs

- Experience with AWS services such as DynamoDB, SQS, SNS, Lambda, and ElastiCache (Redis)

- Experience with notification and engagement platforms (Braze, Amazon Pinpoint, APNs, FCM) or in-app subscription billing (App Store, Google Play)

- Experience with stream processing frameworks such as Apache Flink or Kafka Streams

- Experience with A/B testing platforms (Statsig, LaunchDarkly, Optimizely) and analytics warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake)

- Experience consuming or integrating LLM-based APIs (e.g., Bedrock, Vertex AI, OpenAI)

- Familiarity with Kubernetes, Helm, and CI/CD pipelines

About OfferUp: 

OfferUp is dedicated to creating the simplest and most trusted way for people to buy, sell, and connect in their local communities. One of the top local marketplace apps for local buyers and sellers in the U.S., OfferUp makes it easy for people to discover more of what they need—from great deals and secondhand goods to jobs, services, home rentals, and more—right in their own communities. Our trusted platform empowers millions to connect, thrive, and move life forward. 

Available on iOS and Android, OfferUp has consistently ranked among the top shopping apps. Founded in 2011 and based in Bellevue, WA, OfferUp serves local markets nationwide and was used by more than 1 in 6 adults in the U.S. in 2024. OfferUp is backed by leading investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Warburg Pincus, GGV Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Coatue Management. https://about.offerup.com

More About OfferUp At a Glance

- 15%+ of adults in several major markets use OfferUp every month (LA, Miami, Phoenix, Seattle, Las Vegas, Riverside, Orlando)

- OfferUp works directly with nearly 2000 US law enforcement agencies to build trust in local communities

OfferUp is unleashing the power of local, and we’ve built a dynamic team to do it. To learn more about working at OfferUp, check out https://about.offerup.com/people

Cardog | Toronto, Canada or REMOTE | Full-time
https://cardog.app/careers We're the system of record for the Canadian vehicle: raw automotive data turned into facts that can be checked. Our open-source VIN decoder sits underneath a government vehicle registry. Some of what's interesting: - A government registry, a manufacturer's own filing, a listing site and an insurance record will describe the same truck four different ways, and nothing in any of those files says they're the same truck. Reconciling that, for every vehicle in the country, in a way that holds up when a regulator asks how you know, is most of the data work. - Seventeen characters on a door frame encode manufacturer, plant, model year and build attributes — badly, inconsistently, and differently per manufacturer. Public reference data covers some of it. The rest gets worked out from filings, recall documents, and patterns inferred across millions of vehicles. - We read vehicles directly over OBD-II now. Forty modules answered on a recent Hyundai, each reporting its own part number and installed software version. Nothing downstream of the VIN moves when a module is reflashed, so no registration, history report or dealer system knows what software is actually in a car. This role provides hands-on technical leadership across multiple fireteams, supporting on complex incident response, conducting deep technical case review, identifying operations and product improvement opportunities, and driving technical quality across regional operations through various technical deliverables. The Regional Principal Analyst maintains deep, current expertise through regular hands-on engagement, and collaboration in complex service delivery scenarios.

What You'll Do: 

Technical Leadership: 

- Serve as the principal technical advisor to Regional Directors and Senior Leadership Team on all Falcon Complete service delivery matters 
- Ensure technical consistency, quality standards, and best practices across regional operations 
- Lead regional technical initiatives 
- Coordinate with other Regional Principals to ensure global consistency and knowledge sharing

Technical Escalation Support: 

- Serve as a technical escalation resource for Fireteam Principal Analysts on complex or ambiguous cases, providing second opinion, additional analysis, and technical guidance, while assisting with Principal technical development 
- Fireteam Principal Analysts retain ownership and lead of high-severity incident response; the Regional Principal supports as a technical resource, and highlights opportunities to improve the Falcon Complete service and technical excellence of the region. 
- Perform independent technical analysis when asked to validate or extend a fireteam's findings 

Operational Excellence & Quality Assurance: 

- Conduct technical QA reviews of closed cases across fireteams against defined criteria with documented findings 
- Identify detection gaps, false-positive patterns, and coverage opportunities from regional case data; route findings to relevant teams as improvement requests 
- Identify opportunities for tooling, telemetry, or workflow improvements based on recurring case patterns 
- Identify regional trends in detection patterns, threat landscape, and case quality 
- Identify skill gaps and development opportunities across the regional analyst population 
- Drive adoption of consistent operational standards and agentic toolsets across regional operations. 

Cross-Functional Technical Liaison 

- Represent regional technical perspective in cross-functional initiatives with other CrowdStrike business units 
- Work directly with Product/Engineering to surface detection coverage gaps, platform bugs, and feature requests 
- Coordinate with OverWatch and Intelligence on regional threat trends 
- Partner with other Regional Principal Analysts on shared technical review standards and case QA criteria 
- Partner with Watchtower to drive detection tuning and coverage improvements based on regional intelligence. 

Thought Leadership & Market Engagement 

- Demonstrate industry thought leadership through blog posts, CrowdCasts, conference presentations, and other speaking events as appropriate

Strategic Projects & Innovation 

- Provide Technical expertise on regional projects that align with Falcon Complete mission and corporate goals 
- Drive innovation in detection gaps, triage, remediation, and automation capabilities 
- Collaborate with Section 3 (S3) AI Automation Team on regional automation opportunities 
- Identify and implement efficiency improvements with measurable regional impact 

Supervision & Autonomy

- Expected to remain hands-on

What You'll Need 

Successful candidates will have extensive experience in multiple of the following areas: 

- Incident Handling: expert-level experience leading and managing complex incident response investigations, including the ability to take ownership of high-severity, multi-host, and multi-customer incidents from triage through remediation. Proven experience investigating host/user compromises, organized crime groups, and sophisticated nation-state adversaries.

- Computer Forensic Analysis: advanced experience conducting forensic analysis across host, memory, and network artifacts using a broad toolkit to determine full scope and root cause of compromise. 
- Malware Analysis: advanced ability to perform static and dynamic malware analysis, including reverse engineering concepts and behavioral analysis.

- Identity Platform Awareness: deep expertise with identity and access management platforms such as Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, and Active Directory, including advanced knowledge of identity-based attack techniques and credential abuse patterns. 
- Email Security Awareness: advanced experience investigating and remediating Microsoft 365 security incidents, including sophisticated business email compromise (BEC) and adversary-in-the-middle (AITM) attack chains. 
- Third-Party Log Analysis: advanced proficiency querying and correlating log sources across cloud platforms, network devices, identity providers, and email platforms within a SIEM environment to build detection logic and drive complex investigations.

About DrFirst

For 25 years, DrFirst has empowered providers and patients to achieve better health through intelligent medication management. We improve healthcare workflows and help patients start and stay on therapy with end-to-end solutions that enhance prescription access, affordability, and adherence. Our solutions help 100 million patients a year and are used by more than 420,000 prescribers, 71,000 pharmacies, 270 EHRs and health information systems, and over 2,000 hospitals in the U.S. This is a great opportunity to be a part of a successful Healthcare IT company experiencing significant growth. Here you’ll get to work with some of the smartest and most interesting people around, solving unique and complex challenges in healthcare on a scale matched by few companies. If you get excited about stretching yourself in new ways, developing yourself to your fullest potential, and care about working with smart colleagues, we want to talk to you!

Position Overview

DrFirst is hiring a Senior Software Engineer for the eRx Enterprise and Gadget team. Your first focus is Gadget, our pharmacy agent. Over time you will extend your work into Rcopia, our ePrescribing platform, on Electronic Prescribing of Controlled Substances (EPCS) and Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) workflows.

You will build cloud native, high performance services for an ePrescribing collaboration platform. The platform connects providers, patients, payers, pharmacies, and pharmaceutical companies in real time. You will design systems built for high load, with self healing, auto scaling, and full observability.

You bring strong judgment about AI. You know when AI speeds up delivery and when AI produces weak code. You apply AI to raise code quality, performance, and design standards across the team, and you solve real problems for the pharmacies and prescribers who rely on our platform.

What You Will Work On

- Build and improve Gadget, the DrFirst pharmacy agent, from design through production.

- Design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain secure, scalable Java integration solutions.
- Build cloud native microservices on AWS with auto scaling, fault tolerance, high availability, and self healing.
- Develop and maintain integrations with major EHR platforms, including athenaOne, Epic, Oracle Health, Greenway, AdvancedMD, eMDs, and ModMed, using HL7, FHIR, web services, APIs, and Mirth Connect.
- Build and maintain event driven architectures with Apache Kafka for reliable, efficient service communication.
- Deliver high throughput and low latency across large, distributed platforms.
- Partner with DevOps on CI/CD pipelines that automate testing, deployment, and monitoring.
- Design AI powered automation frameworks for faster development cycles and automated regression testing.
- Decide where AI adds value in the codebase and where human design must lead. Set review standards for AI assisted code.
- Monitor, diagnose, and resolve performance issues with observability tools and logs.
- Follow and enforce secure coding practices. Take part in security audits and reviews.
- Lead code reviews, mentor junior developers, and contribute to architecture decisions.
- Track industry trends and improve system performance, resilience, and developer productivity.

Qualifications

Required

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related discipline.
- 5+ years of hands on Java development with deep knowledge of object oriented design and the Spring Framework, including Spring Boot and Spring Cloud.
- 3+ years designing and building cloud native applications on AWS, including S3, Valkey, Lambda, RDS, and EKS or ECS.
- 3+ years with distributed messaging systems such as Apache Kafka, with a solid grasp of event streaming.
- Proven record building and integrating large scale, high performance, distributed systems with fault tolerance, scalability, and low latency.
- AI first mindset, with daily hands on use of AI tools such as Claude and GitHub Copilot for coding, testing, debugging, and documentation.
- Clear judgment on when and where AI improves engineering outcomes, and a record of keeping AI generated code from lowering quality, performance, or design.
- Proficiency building and consuming RESTful APIs with JSON and XML.
- Strong experience with relational or NoSQL databases, including schema design, performance tuning, and query optimization.
- Hands on experience with CI/CD pipelines and tools such as GitLab CI and Jenkins.
- Solid knowledge of application and data security, including authentication, authorization, and data protection.
- Self motivated. You work well on your own in a fast paced, agile environment.
- Fast learner who adapts to new technologies, teams, and environments.
- Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills with a proactive, solution oriented approach.

Preferred

- Experience building AI agents, LLM integrations, or agentic workflows in production.
- Experience with large scale, mission critical systems in finance, brokerage, trading, or credit card processing, especially systems requiring low latency, high throughput, and high availability.
- Experience with ePrescribing, EPCS, PDMP, NCPDP SCRIPT, or pharmacy systems.
- Familiarity with front end technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript).

Physical Requirements

- Primarily desk work in a remote, U.S. based setting.
- Extended periods of computer use.

Harmonic exists to help enterprises adopt AI safely and at scale. We hold ourselves to that same standard. Everyone here actively leverages AI tools to perform their best work, from deep research and writing to building robust processes and automating complex workflows. We expect every new hire to bring a genuine curiosity for AI and a commitment to using it to work smarter, faster, and with greater creativity.
